item.title: Hong Kong like a local
item.dc:creator: Farah Master
item.content:encoded: REUTERS/Illustration/Kate Evans Hong Kong — which means “fragrant harbour” in Chinese — is known for its glistening financial centre and densely packed skyline. But beneath this glimmering facade lies another Hong Kong: one of sprawling, green country parks, world-class hiking, and over 260 islands that form a paradise for open-water swimming. I was born and raised here, and after stints for Reuters in London, Beijing and Shanghai, returned here in 2013 to cover breaking news. I grew up hiking Hong Kong’s nature trails, taking my golden retriever swimming at local beaches and tucking into bamboo baskets of char siu bao (barbecued pork bun) and har gao (shrimp dumplings). While the city’s political fabric has shifted dramatically following 2019 pro-democracy protests , the passage of a 2020 national security law and the COVID-19 pandemic, Hong Kong is beginning to regain its mojo, drawing back international visitors and expatriates alike. Here’s how to explore Hong Kong like a local: The way around: Hong Kong boasts one of the world’s cleanest and most efficient public transportation networks. It begins with the Airport Express train , which whisks you from the international airport straight into the Central business district in just 24 minutes, with fares costing up to HK$130 ($16.50). Tourists take selfies along the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu A woman holding incense walks through Man Mo Temple. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu People walk along a street in Hong Kong's Soho district, decorated with temporary neon lights and market stalls for a film production. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu A Peak Tram car ascends towards Victoria Peak with the Hong Kong skyline in the background. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu Tourists walk past stalls selling Hong Kong-themed souvenirs at the Ladies' Market in Hong Kong's Mong Kok district. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu Tourists walk past stalls at the Ladies' Market in Hong Kong's Mong Kok district. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu Tourists board a sightseeing boat on Victoria Harbour. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu Tourists watch the sunset over Victoria Harbour. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu People walk along a street in Hong Kong's Soho district, decorated with temporary neon lights and market stalls for a film production. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu Tourists ride a Star Ferry with Hong Kong's Central financial district in the background, China, July 24, 2026. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu A tram passes the Court of Final Appeal in Hong Kong's Central district. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu A dog walks past people on Repulse Bay Beach. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu Tourists take pictures of Hong Kong's skyline from Victoria Peak. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu The underground rail network, the Mass Transit Railway (MTR) , is so famously punctual that if a train pauses for even 30 seconds longer than scheduled, an automated announcement immediately apologises and asks passengers for their patience. Air-conditioned double-decker buses traverse the entire territory, while the tram — known locally as the “ding ding” — is a charming, slow-paced way to take in the sounds, smells and sights of Hong Kong Island. Visitors can pay for both using an Octopus card (buy it at the airport, MTR customer service centres or convenience stores like 7-Eleven) or by using contactless payment. For a more scenic journey, board the historic Star Ferry , connecting Hong Kong Island to the bustling Kowloon peninsula, or hop on a ferry out to the tranquil outlying islands of Lantau or Lamma. Into nature: For a classic introduction to Hong Kong’s peaks, take a stroll up the Morning Trail from Hatton Road to Victoria Peak, where you can find incredible views of Victoria Harbour. From there, you could continue up to Victoria Peak Garden , a quiet Victorian-style park featuring open lawns and panoramic views. To head back down to Central, ride the historic Peak Tram , one of the world’s oldest funicular railways, which climbs gradients of up to 25.7 degrees. Repulse Bay , a 20-minute bus ride from Central, is a favourite year-round beach spot. After swimming, grab a coffee or tea at Neighbourhood , just across from the beach, or a bite at one of the many beachside cafes. For a scenic day hike, try the Dragon’s Back , an 8km (5-mile) trail that snakes along the ridge of Shek O Peak and descends to the white sands of Big Wave Bay, a popular surf spot adjacent to Shek O village and its laid-back eateries. If time permits, a trip to Tai Long Wan bay on the Sai Kung peninsula is also a must. With its turquoise waters and pristine beaches, you could easily mistake it for a Thai island. The easiest way to access it is via a speedboat from Sai Kung town, though be warned it can be a bit choppy on the water. Alternatively, you can hike in via several scenic routes from Sai Kung country park. Shopping spree: While many locals travel across the border to Shenzhen for shopping, Hong Kong remains a retail hub. For electronics, head to the Wan Chai Computer Centre . For sneakers and streetwear, try Fa Yuen Street (known as Sneakers Street) in Mong Kok. If you're looking for vibrant neighbourhood culture, explore Sham Shui Po’s independent shops and quirky cafes. Or beat the subtropical heat in air-conditioned malls like Pacific Place, IFC and Times Square. Get artsy: Hong Kong has rapidly expanded its arts offerings over the years, most notably with the contemporary art M+ Museum and the Hong Kong Palace Museum , which offers Chinese historical artwork as well as special exhibitions including ancient Egyptian civilisations in West Kowloon. The underground rail network, the Mass Transit Railway (MTR), is so famously punctual that if a train pauses for even 30 seconds longer than scheduled, an automated announcement immediately apologises and asks passengers for their patience. On Hong Kong island, Tai Kwun is a meticulously restored colonial-era police station turned heritage and arts centre. Nearby, the historic Fringe Club hosts indie art exhibitions and live music. For a unique architectural experience, visit the Asia Society in Admiralty, housed within former 19th-century British military buildings. Good eats: From Dai pai dongs (open-air food stalls) to world-class fine dining, Hong Kong is a culinary powerhouse. While the Chinese food is stellar, the city’s international community ensures access to excellent Thai, Japanese, Korean, Indian and Lebanese cuisine as well. For dim sum, Tim Ho Wan remains a budget-friendly favourite, while Lin Heung Tea House offers a nostalgic experience where servers wheel traditional metal trolleys piled high with bamboo steamer baskets. For a more upscale experience, head to Madam Fu at Tai Kwun for contemporary Cantonese cuisine. I recommend trying the smoked bean curd roll with shiitake mushroom and carrot and the wagyu beef mapo tofu. If you are craving Southeast Asian flavours, Samsen serves delicious flat beef or vegetable rice noodles, while Arirang does a great traditional Korean barbecue. CITY MEMO DATA POINTS Population: 7.5 million people Price of a coffee: HK$35 ($5) for a macchiato at Frenchies on Hollywood Road or HK$30 ($3.80) for a coffee at local chain Fineprint. Price of an ice cream: HK$58 ($7.40) for a scoop at Snack Baby Gelato , which has unique local flavours including Szechuan chilli mango and five-spice mandarin. Great place to see a sunset: Tsim Sha Tsui promenade offers great views of the Hong Kong skyline at night. Largest university: University of Hong Kong, 45,000 students

item.title: Jay Rayner on the responsibility of restaurant criticism
item.description: The veteran British food critic discusses his new book, how the pandemic changed his approach to negative reviews, and the places he won’t cover.
item.dc:creator: Yasmeen Serhan
item.content:encoded: British food critic Jay Rayner poses for a photograph at his home in London, Britain, August 19, 2026. REUTERS/Hannah McKay Jay Rayner, by his own admission, doesn’t get invited to too many dinner parties. The veteran British restaurant critic — whose more than a quarter-century of reviews for The Observer and, more recently, the Financial Times newspaper has earned him the nickname “Acid Rayner” — is known for his searing assessments of restaurants across the U.K. Among his most excoriating assessments was that he couldn’t describe one place as serving “the worst cooking in Britain,” if only because he hadn’t eaten in every restaurant in the land. But Rayner’s day job doesn’t mean he’ll turn his nose up atgood old-fashioned home cooking, which he pays homage to in his latest book “Nights Out in the Kitchen,” a part-cookbook, part-memoir featuring recipes for some of the best dishes from across his career, plus some original dishes. Speaking with Reuters from his home in South London ahead of his book tour , Rayner discusses the art of the review in the social media age, his philosophy for negative critiques, and the restaurants he won’t go near. This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity. British food critic Jay Rayner poses for a photograph at his home in London, Britain, August 19, 2026. REUTERS/Hannah McKay You’ve been a restaurant critic for more than a quarter century. How’d you get your start? I’m a print journalist. That is the thing I've always been. I chose my university because it had the biggest student newspaper, got elected editor, and I was then a general writer and reporter, advancing from very soft features into harder and harder news and long form and foreign reporting. I did it all apart from sport — and even then, I like to point out that I once did the all-amateur natural bodybuilding championship in Leeds. And then, (in 1999), I was taken out for lunch by the then editor of The Observer magazine, for whom I deputized on every column, and she said, "Our restaurant critic is moving on. Who should I get to do the job?" It was not my intention to put my hand up. But the moment she said that, I went, "Well, how about me?" What I discovered in food was that it covers everything: politics, economics, history, trade routes. When people look at the Arab Spring, they see it as a spontaneous uprising in response to a sudden desire for democracy. But if you drill down on it, it's actually about food price rises and the inability of authoritarian governments to keep their population in line when they could no longer give them bread at a reasonable price. And when you start to understand that, you think, this is a really interesting subject. And so it has continually become a part of my working life. Over 25 years, what's changed about what makes a good review? And what has stayed the same? Has anything changed about what makes a good review? I don't think it has, actually. I think the eternal verities (remain true), which is that you have to speak to the reader as though they're the only person reading, that you are telling them how much pleasure their money will give them. You're not writing for the tiny number of well-informed gastronomes — the "napkin sniffers," as I call them — but for the general reader and you need to understand it as a conversation with those readers. What I discovered in food was that it covers everything: politics, economics, history, trade routes Jay Rayner That said, a lot has changed about the way restaurants are covered, how much other coverage there is. Social media has played a big part in that. With the rise of content creation, these days most anyone can be a critic. Do you see that as a challenge? It is only a challenge if it's better than me. I cannot just claim, "Look, I'm the guy from the big newspaper and therefore I have a right to be read." Every writer has to make an argument for their writing to be read every single time they write. Nobody has to read a single thing you write — not even your mother. There's a lot of stuff out there, and some of it's good and some of it's bad. Generally, I like to think that the audience will spot the rubbish. There are certain influencer review sites where I think, "Oh God, this is awful,” but it's got 2.5 million followers, so they must like something about it. Your new book reads as part-cookbook, part memoir. What are you hoping readers take from it, apart from some delicious home cooking recipes? This is the sequel to "Nights Out at Home," which happened because I was heading towards 25 years (as a restaurant critic), and what I realized was I genuinely have this habit of, if I come across a good idea in a restaurant, I'll take it home and reverse engineer that idea. I thought, actually, that's a brilliant way (of) telling the stories of these restaurants you love. It's a very broad selection of dishes, plus, with this one, 20 of the (recipes) are officially mine. They're things that I cook or have always cooked. In one chapter, you reflect on some of the more brutal reviews you’ve given. You mean the chapter headed, "Am I a total bastard?" British food critic Jay Rayner poses for a photograph with his new book Nights Out in the Kitchen, at his home in London, Britain, August 19, 2026. REUTERS/Hannah McKay That's the one. It got me wondering: How do you approach writing a negative review? Have you ever returned to a restaurant that received one to see if it improved? I've done it only once. It was a place where they’d advertised themselves as being a great Italian new wave restaurant. I went there and concluded it was just a bar, and they weren't really interested in the food. That was the review. The owner wrote to me and said, "You're absolutely right, but we are now," and I went back and it was. The interesting thing, at least to me, is I wouldn't have bothered with that first review now. If I'd gone there and had that experience, I would have paid the bill and never written about it. So the major difference now, and I think it's a lot to do with COVID and coming out of (the pandemic), is if you're going to write a negative review, you better have a bloody good reason for it. And the motto is: punch up, not down. The small mom-and-pop place that's not doing very well or isn't making it, let them fail by themselves. But if you come across somewhere like (the high-end London restaurant) Jul's — this mad, insane place apparently born out of some landmark restaurant in Ibiza where they were doing terrible things to the food at excruciating prices, I didn't have any concerns about writing what I felt . And the point I said in the review was: money might end up being spent here that should be spent elsewhere. Now that's a bit brutal, but it's true. You write about the #MeToo reckoning in kitchens. Has that changed how you review a restaurant — what you're looking for, what you're weighing? It is complicated because, generally, you do not know what's going on in a restaurant. It's like a family: You can't necessarily tell it's dysfunctional if you just go over for tea. Maybe you can sense it. There are certain chefs I will not review because I think they're monstrous individuals. If you are a nightmarish figure, I'm not going near you. That all sounds very grand and moral. The problem is you can't always tell. What kinds of cuisines do you think are still unrepresented or underrepresented in the places you review? The entirety of Africa. We obviously have very developed African communities in the U.K., but the restaurants representing the food of Africa tend to be mediated in some way. Sichuan food (in London) will bear similarities to what you find in Chengdu, whereas a Nigerian restaurant that ends up in Soho is unlikely to be what you'll find in the back streets of Lagos. I'm not sure why that is. Now for some rapid-fire questions. What’s your death-row meal? You can find it in my book, "My Last Supper: One Meal, a Lifetime in the Making." It would involve garlicky snails, a bacon sandwich properly made on white bread, and a Mont Blanc to finish. Who would you invite to your dream dinner party? Dorothy Parker, but only until the end of the starters, because after that she'll be drunk and just a bit annoying. Peter Ustinov, who was a great British actor, wit, and raconteur. Ella Fitzgerald, because I have a sideline as a jazz pianist and I'd love to play alongside her. Gene Harris, who is a fantastic, bluesy jazz pianist. And if I'm allowed fictional, Baloo the Bear from "The Jungle Book." Another is Dita Von Teese. After Dorothy Parker has had to retire, Dita can take over. What’s your favorite restaurant of late? My most recent top experience is a place called IGNI . It is a live-fire tasting menu restaurant (in London) by a chef called Theo Clench. I normally have no time or patience for the whole tasting menu thing — I find it tiresome and performative, and all the performance doesn't match up to the joy of the food. But this one really, really did. The perspectives expressed in Culture Current are the subject’s own and do not necessarily reflect the views of Reuters News.

item.title: En Irlande pour un tournoi de golf, Trump "adorerait" voir l'île réunifiée
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré samedi à Dublin qu'il "adorerait" que l'Irlande soit réunifiée, avant de se rendre dans l'ouest du pays pour assister à un tournoi de golf dans l'un de ses complexes hôteliers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré samedi à Dublin qu'il "adorerait" que l'Irlande soit réunifiée, avant de se rendre dans l'ouest du pays pour assister à un tournoi de golf dans l'un de ses complexes hôteliers. Le président américain a fait cette déclaration à la presse à l'issue d'entretiens avec les dirigeants irlandais et alors que le Premier ministre britannique, Andy Burnham, a exclu il y a quelques semaines la tenue d'un référendum sur la sortie de l'Irlande du Nord du Royaume-uni. "Eh bien, je ne veux pas causer de problèmes, mais je vais vous dire : j'adorerais voir cette réunification se réaliser", a déclaré Donald Trump à la presse après s'être entretenu avec le Premier ministre irlandais Micheal Martin. "Cela finira par arriver... Je pense que ce serait formidable." "Le Royaume-Uni aura bien sûr son mot à dire à ce sujet, mais je pense que ce serait une excellente chose", a-t-il ajouté. Aux termes des accords de paix du Vendredi Saint qui ont mis fin en 1998 à trois décennies de guerre civile, le gouvernement britannique est seul habilité à convoquer un référendum sur la réunification de l'Irlande. Donald Trump a fait cette déclaration alors qu'il était assailli de questions sur les conséquences économiques de la guerre au Moyen-Orient, dont il n'arrive pas à se dépêtrer. Des manifestations contre la guerre et contre sa venue en Irlande étaient d'ailleurs prévues plus tard dans la journée à Dublin et dans l'ouest du pays, où le président américain doit remettre le trophée au vainqueur de l'Irish Open de golf, qui s'achèvera dimanche sur le parcours de Doonbeg, propriété de la Trump Organization. L'Irlande est l'un des pays de l'Union européenne les plus anti-guerre et pro-palestiniens. Dublin a adopté en juillet une loi restreignant le commerce de marchandises avec les colonies en Cisjordanie occupée par Israël, ce qui lui a valu de vives critiques américaines. D'autres pays européens, dont la Grande-Bretagne et la France, se sont depuis associés à ces sanctions. Micheal Martin a jusqu'à présent réussi à éviter tout clash public avec Donald Trump. "Les relations entre l'Irlande et les États-Unis sont très importantes sur le plan économique", a-t-il rappelé avant son arrivée. Le président américain a également être reçu samedi à Dublin par son homologue irlandaise Catherine Connolly. Élue l'an dernier, la dirigeante de gauche connue pour son franc-parler avait participé en 2019 à une manifestation contre la précédente visite de Donald Trump en Irlande.

item.title: BRICS agrees to joint declaration in test of unity despite Mideast tensions
item.description: It is a significant diplomatic breakthrough as its leaders hold talks in New Delhi, hoping to build their global clout and bridge divisions between Iran and the UAE.
item.dc:creator: Sarita Singh, Shivangi Acharya, Saurabh Sharma
item.content:encoded: The BRICS group of emerging economies has agreed on a joint declaration, sources told Reuters on Saturday, a significant diplomatic breakthrough as its leaders began summit talks in New Delhi, aiming to boost the bloc's global clout. Host India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the bloc had come of age and it was time to translate its unity and consensus into concrete results on the global stage, as he opened the meeting. The summit, hoping to bridge divisions between members Iran and the United Arab Emirates over the Gulf conflict, is being held as the United States and Iran resume [USN:L6N45203X TEXT:"tit-for-tat strikes"] in their six-month-old war. That followed a pause in fighting for much of August, while the Iran-aligned Houthi rebels in Yemen [USN:L6N453173 TEXT:"tightened their grip"] in the Red Sea region. Negotiators had agreed on a joint declaration unlikely to name any country but which will condemn unilateral aggression by any country, four sources told Reuters, adding that the bloc's leaders were expected to approve the document later on Saturday. The sources declined to be identified as they are not authorised to speak to the media. The foreign ministry of host India did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the declaration. The negotiations saw differences on several contentious issues but India led sustained consultations to bridge competing positions and build consensus among members, said an Indian source with direct knowledge of the development. Against the backdrop of ongoing conflicts and heightened tensions in the Gulf region, securing consensus presented a particularly complex diplomatic challenge, the source said. PUTIN, XI, PEZESHKIAN, RAMAPHOSA IN ATTENDANCE Foreign policy experts had said the key test for the bloc would be finding language on the Middle East crisis that both Abu Dhabi and Tehran could accept, clearing the way for a joint declaration. Such a joint statement was unlikely to influence the current geopolitical landscape, but would demonstrate unity by a grouping of emerging nations against economically debilitating policies such as Western sanctions, they said. BRICS [USN:FWN41R1LK TEXT:"foreign ministers"] meeting in New Delhi in May were unable to issue a joint statement, stymied by differences between Iran and the UAE. The BRICS bloc is seeking to raise its profile by influencing international rules and demanding the reform of institutions such as the World Bank, International Monetary Fund and World Trade Organization, which some members view as being dominated by Western powers. Leaders attending the summit are Russian President Vladimir Putin, China's Xi Jinping, Iran's Masoud Pezeshkian, South Africa's Cyril Ramaphosa and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, among others. Chinese President Xi said BRICS countries should firmly stand on the right side of history by steering the international order toward greater equity and justice. New Delhi, which has strong ties with the United States, Russia, Israel, Iran and the Gulf Arab states, is engaged in a diplomatic balancing act, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi pushing BRICS members to boost trade cooperation, reduce barriers and expand business opportunities. EVERY COUNTRY SHOULD HAVE A VOICE, MODI SAYS "While strengthening BRICS, we must also determine the direction of global reform," Modi said. "The Global South is today in the front row when it comes to global crises, but in the back row when it comes to decision-making. We have to transform this pyramid and privilege into a platform of partnership — where every country has a voice, every member has a stake." Modi also reiterated India's longstanding demand for expansion of the U.N. Security Council, including permanent seats for itself and other emerging powers, saying that reform of the Security Council can no longer be delayed. "The message of this BRICS Summit being held in India should be clear: If our future is shared, then the right to shape that future must also be shared," Modi said. BRICS groups Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates. It was [USN:L6N4510UT TEXT:"set up"] in 2009 to challenge a world order dominated by the United States and its Western allies. Together, its members account for more than 40% of the world's population and almost a quarter of the global economy.

item.title: Pirates ace Paul Skenes hopes for better outcome vs. Cubs
item.description: Alex Bregman has been heating up since the All-Star break, and Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell couldn't be happier.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alex Bregman has been heating up since the All-Star break, and Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell couldn't be happier. The three-time All-Star will look to continue his hot hitting on Saturday afternoon as the Cubs chase a series victory against the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates. Bregman belted a two-run homer and finished a triple shy of the cycle on Friday afternoon, helping Chicago cruise to a 12-2 romp over Pittsburgh in the opener of a three-game series. The homer was Bregman's 25th of the season and 16th since the All-Star break. "It's kind of been a tale of two halves for him. And that's just the way it is this year," Counsell said. "We're glad the second half is going this way, and we have some games to go with him playing like this. He's had an Alex Bregman season. ... He's doing what we'd hoped he would do." Bregman wasn't the only one to swing a hot bat on Friday. Michael Busch drove in three runs and Seiya Suzuki scored three runs and joined Bregman with three hits for the Cubs (82-66), who banged out 16 hits en route to snapping a four-game skid. Chicago is tied with the Philadelphia Phillies (82-66) for the National League's top wild-card spot. The Cubs are expected to be tested on Saturday afternoon against reigning NL Cy Young Award winner Paul Skenes (10-11, 3.83 ERA). Skenes scattered four hits over 5 1/3 scoreless innings in a 1-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Sunday. The win was the first for the right-hander since July 19, ending a seven-outing winless run. Skenes has struggled in two starts versus the Cubs this season, going 0-2 with a 5.06 ERA. All told, he is 2-4 with a 3.45 ERA in nine career appearances (all starts) against Chicago. Cubs right-hander Clay Holmes (6-7, 2.83 ERA) is expected to get the nod on Saturday. Holmes strung together four consecutive strong outings before getting shelled for eight runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings of a 10-3 setback to the Miami Marlins on Sunday. Holmes, a former Pirate, is 0-1 with a 4.22 ERA in six career appearances (one start) versus Pittsburgh. Rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin tripled and singled on Friday for the Pirates (74-74), who likely will be without Esmerlyn Valdez. The rookie right fielder left the Friday game in the sixth inning due to left hamstring discomfort. Valdez's departure came on the same day that Pittsburgh welcomed back Ryan O'Hearn, who was activated off the 10-day injured list. He had been sidelined since July 31 with a left quad injury. "You love when guys want to push it to get back and just to make sure that he's in a good spot to be able to do that," Pirates manager Don Kelly said of O'Hearn, who went 0-for-2 on Friday after entering the game as a pinch hitter. "Confident in him being able to be Ryan O'Hearn and have good at-bats and be able to move around like he does." Pirates rookie catcher Rafael Flores Jr. carries a career-best six-game hitting streak into the Saturday contest. --Field Level Media

item.title: Philippines begins identifying victims from ferry fire as dozens still missing
item.description: Philippine authorities began the painstaking process of identifying victims from a ferry fire on Saturday, a day after responders recovered bodies from the burned-out vessel, raising the death toll to at least 35 and leaving more than 50 people missing.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Portugal, Eloisa Lopez
item.content:encoded: Philippine authorities began the painstaking process of identifying victims from a ferry fire on Saturday, a day after responders [USN:L6N45307E TEXT:"recovered bodies"] from the burned-out vessel, raising the death toll to at least 35 and leaving more than 50 people missing. The bodies were transported to a port in Coron town, where temporary tents were set up for forensic teams to process and identify the victims. Near the port, some family members anxiously watched as responders in protective suits carried black body bags from a Coast Guard vessel to temporary tents. One of them was Anelyn Magbanua, 37, whose husband was returning to Coron after visiting their children in Manila when the ferry, which was carrying more than 130 people, caught fire near the end of its more than 20-hour journey. "I hope he is not among the dead being brought off the ship. I hope he is alive and has only drifted to another island," she said. "It will be very difficult to accept if he's really gone," she said. "He loved his children very much." Firefighters entered the ferry for the first time on Friday after extinguishing the blaze more than a day after it broke out, giving authorities access to areas that had been hard to reach because of thick smoke and extreme heat. The Coast Guard said burnt remains were discovered in the ferry's economy accommodation section. Images released by the Coast Guard showed the scale of the destruction inside the vessel, with rows of steel bed frames twisted by intense heat and blanketed in ash. Some photographs appeared to show skeletal remains among the debris. Philippine Coast Guard official Geronimo Tuvilla said at a press conference on Saturday that the immediate priority was to identify the victims and determine the cause of the fire. A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority, citing survivor accounts, said two explosions were heard inside the vessel shortly before the fire broke out. One survivor interviewed by GMA News recalled seeing a small amount of smoke that turned into a fire and quickly spread through the ferry within seconds. Questions also remained over the fate of the vessel's captain. Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said at the same press conference that she had received information that he was alive, but added that the captain's name was not on the list of 43 confirmed survivors. The fire is the latest in a string of deadly maritime accidents in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands where millions rely on ferries and small boats to travel between provinces and islands.

item.title: BRICS bloc agrees on joint declaration, sources say
item.description: The BRICS group of countries has agreed on a joint declaration, which is unlikely to name any country but will condemn unilateral war by any country, four sources told Reuters on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The BRICS group of countries has agreed on a joint declaration, which is unlikely to name any country but will condemn unilateral war by any country, four sources told Reuters on Saturday. The bloc, which includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, is holding its annual summit in New Delhi this weekend. Representatives of the member nations have been engaged on bridging the divide between Iran and the United Arab Emirates, who are on opposite sides of the Gulf conflict, to produce a consensus declaration. The leaders of the countries are expected to approve the declaration on Saturday, the sources said.

item.title: Andrew Sears set to rejoin Tigers for start against Rockies
item.description: The Detroit Tigers traded a two-time Cy Young Award-winning pitcher and tumbled out of the playoff race last month. A jolt of youth and energy has given them hope for the future.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Tigers traded a two-time Cy Young Award-winning pitcher and tumbled out of the playoff race last month. A jolt of youth and energy has given them hope for the future. Detroit, which hosts the Colorado Rockies on Saturday afternoon in the second game of a three-game series, has won four of its last six games. Infielder Kevin McGonigle appears headed for the American League Rookie of the Year award, and center fielder Max Clark is among numerous prospects getting extended playing time as the season winds down. Clark belted a solo homer on Friday and scored another run after getting hit by a pitch. He stole second, then reached third and home on wild pitches in Detroit's 6-2, series-opening victory. "When you see him running in open speed, he's top-tier speed," manager A.J. Hinch said. "And he's going to learn how to use it and trust that he can do even more than what he's doing now. And that's exciting." Another rookie, left-hander Andrew Sears (0-1, 4.38 ERA), is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Toledo to make a spot start for Detroit on Saturday. He will be facing the Rockies for the first time. Sears was optioned after his first career start on Sept. 4, when he held the Cleveland Guardians to one run and four hits in 5 2/3 innings during a no-decision. "Definitely felt good," he said after that contest. "I was back in my own routine and in my element. Definitely just attacked it like any other start." And Sears likes to attack quickly. He wastes little time between pitches. "It just keeps the hitters dialed in," he said. "They don't like working fast. They're trying to use the clock against me. But as soon as they look at me, I'm throwing the ball." Sears is 3-2 with a 2.16 ERA in 16 games, including 12 starts, in the minors this season. He is a candidate to win a starting job with the Tigers next spring. "He can handle the moment and the responsibility," Hinch said. "(The Sept. 4 start) was even more impressive because he knew going into the game he was going to be leaned on quite a bit. It's the most pitches he's thrown this year, and he knew he had to carry the lion's share of the workload." Right-hander Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.40 ERA) will get the ball for the Rockies. He will be making his 10th start to go with 12 long-relief stints. Gordon has pitched at least three innings in all but one of his appearances this season. After giving up just one run in each of his last two August starts, Gordon was rocked for five runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings by the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday. He is 0-2 with a 10.24 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers. The Rockies, who have lost five straight, produced 10 hits during the series opener but left nine men on base. Zac Veen, who finished 1-for-2 after entering in the seventh inning, drove in a ninth-inning run with an infield hit. "I like doing whatever I can to help the team win," said Veen, who comes off the bench more than he starts. "Every game you might get one or two moments to make an impact." --Field Level Media

item.title: Yankees look to continue offensive surge against rival Mets
item.description: The New York Yankees are starting to get going on offense, and they hope to continue their productivity at the plate Saturday afternoon when they host the New York Mets.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Yankees are starting to get going on offense, and they hope to continue their productivity at the plate Saturday afternoon when they host the New York Mets. The Yankees (85-62) are 17-7 in their past 24 games and enter Saturday three games behind the first-place Tampa Bay Rays (88-59) in the American League East and 5 1/2 games ahead of the Boston Red Sox (80-68) for the AL's top wild-card spot. After totaling 13 hits on Friday in a 6-4 win over the Mets following a pregame ceremony to mark the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks, the Yankees are hitting .264 with 31 homers while scoring 126 runs in their past 24 games. The Yankees have totaled 27 runs and 39 hits during a four-game winning streak that coincides with Aaron Judge's return from a fractured right rib that cost him 84 games. The Yankees went 45-39 in his absence. "I'm encouraged," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "For much of the season offensively, from that kind of middle of the season until a few weeks ago, no hiding it, it was a grind for us. A couple of months of really struggling. We're winning games but on the strength of just doing winning things late. "So I do feel like we're finding our stride a little bit offensively. Obviously we're a lot more whole now with not only getting Aaron but a couple of other guys back in the mix, and I feel like there's a lot of different places we can hurt you in the lineup now and we need to keep that going, but it does feel like we're building to a good place offensively." Cody Bellinger hit a three-run homer for the Yankees on Friday and Ben Rice added a solo shot as both players continued their hot streaks. Bellinger is hitting .377 (20-for-53) in his past 13 games while Rice is batting .338 (23-for-68) in his past 17. The Mets (68-79) scored 35 runs during a four-game winning streak that included a 15-14 win over the Miami Marlins on Wednesday. However, they were held to seven hits and went 1-for-6 with runners in scoring position in the opener at Yankee Stadium. Juan Soto struck out twice and also hit into a game-ending double play. He finished 1-for-5, and he has six hits in his past 30 at-bats (.200). Francisco Lindor is in a 5-for-28 (.179) slump after lining out with the bases loaded in the seventh and going 1-for-5. Mets rookie A.J. Ewing is hitting .545 (12-for-22) in his past six games after homering. He also has reached base safely in 10 straight games. "I thought the ceremony was great and I thought it was super cool to see the fans get together for it," Ewing said. Gerrit Cole (8-8, 3.41 ERA) starts for the Yankees on Saturday, hoping to avoid a repeat of his 4-3 loss at San Diego on Sunday. He allowed three straight homers to the Padres' Fernando Tatis Jr., Jake Cronenworth and Manny Machado to start the first inning. Cole later served up a solo shot to Luis Campusano. He permitted four runs on six hits while completing seven innings, tied for his longest outing of the season. The right-hander is 2-4 with a 6.99 ERA in nine career starts against the Mets. Mets left-hander Zac Thornton (3-5, 3.53 ERA) will make his 13th career start and first against the Yankees. He has allowed three earned runs or fewer in 10 starts but is coming off yielding six runs on seven hits, including four homers, in five innings during a 9-5 loss to the San Francisco Giants on Sept. 5. --Field Level Media

item.title: Meloni sees Italy 2026 growth at 1%, matching euro zone
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expects Italy's economy to grow by 1% this year, in line with the euro zone, she said in an interview with newspaper Il Foglio published on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expects Italy's economy to grow by 1% this year, in line with the euro zone, she said in an interview with newspaper Il Foglio published on Saturday. Meloni's government in April forecast 2026 gross domestic product growth of 0.6%, but budget watchdog UPB last month issued a [USN:L8N4410YQ TEXT:"more upbeat projection"] of 0.9%. "The Italian economy is holding up well, and data from the first six months of the year could point to 2026 growth of 1%, in line with, if not above, that of the euro zone," Meloni told Il Foglio. Italian GDP rose by 0.3% quarter-on-quarter in January to March and by 0.2% in the second quarter. So-called "acquired growth" stood at 0.8% at the end of June, meaning that even if GDP is flat in each of the remaining two quarters of 2026, full-year growth will be up 0.8% from 2025. "It is also true that the Italian economy has struggled for many years to achieve sustained and steady growth," Meloni added, citing energy costs and low productivity among the reasons. "We are working to address these issues, but the results of those efforts will only become visible over the medium term," she said. The Italian economy grew 0.5% in 2025. It hasn't exceeded 1% in the last three years despite the steady influx of tens of billions of euros of COVID-19 recovery funds from the European Union.

item.title: Ford to recall about 223,500 US vehicles over fuel tank issues
item.description: Ford is recalling 223,472 vehicles in the U.S. due to leaky and improperly secured fuel tanks that may detach from the vehicle while driving, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ford (F.N) is recalling 223,472 vehicles in the U.S. due to leaky and improperly secured fuel tanks that may detach from the vehicle while driving, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Saturday. Here are some more details from the NHTSA advisory: A detached tank can create a road hazard, increasing the risk of a crash, while a fuel leak can cause an engine stall or increase the risk of a fire. Certain 2023-2027 F-150 vehicles will be recalled due to this concern. Dealers will inspect and replace the fuel tank straps, as necessary, free of charge.

item.title: India's markets regulator proposes revamp of derivatives expiry pricing
item.description: India's markets regulator proposed on Saturday a review of how settlement prices for index and stock derivatives are determined on expiry day.
item.dc:creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: India's markets regulator proposed on Saturday a review of how settlement prices for index and stock derivatives are determined on expiry day. The plans were unveiled in a consultation paper laying out changes to the newly launched Closing Auction Session (CAS) that has led to sharp [USN:L4N44S0W8 TEXT:"market swings"] on derivatives expiry days. The CAS framework was introduced in the equity cash segment for stocks on which derivatives contracts are available, with effect from August 3. The move aimed at efficient and transparent discovery of the closing price of securities. Here are details: • The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has floated two options for expiry-day settlement price of index and stock derivatives. • The first option would blend trades from the last 30 minutes of normal trading with the 10-minute closing auction to yield the settlement price. • The second option would go back to using only the last 30 minutes of normal trading, leaving out the closing auction from the calculation altogether, at least for a year. • The second option would effectively de-link derivatives settlement from CAS for at least a year • The other proposals include barring cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1% above or below the reference price, reducing to five minutes from ten the post-closing auction window for derivatives trading, and not disseminating indicative index close levels during the closing auction. • The regulator has proposed to continue disseminating indicative equilibrium price for stocks during the closing auction. • The regulator invited submission of public comments on the proposals by October 3. • "SEBI is not backing away from CAS. Instead, it is trying to refine CAS after observing expiry-day behaviour," said Rajesh Palviya, senior vice president and head of research at Axis Securities. • "The key objective is to reduce the disconnect between cash-market price discovery and derivatives trading near the close," Palviya said.

item.title: MLB roundup: Rays, Brewers become first teams to clinch playoff berths
item.description: Junior Caminero launched a mammoth walk-off home run in the ninth inning Friday night, sending the Tampa Bay Rays to the postseason by virtue of a 3-1 win over the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Junior Caminero launched a mammoth walk-off home run in the ninth inning Friday night, sending the Tampa Bay Rays to the postseason by virtue of a 3-1 win over the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla. The American League's home run leader, Caminero crushed a 417-foot blast to left-center field off reliever Bryan Abreu (6-4) for his 40th long ball. One batter earlier, Jonathan Aranda nearly homered to right-center, settling for a one-out double. Caminero then belted Abreu's 97 mph first-pitch fastball for his first career walk-off blast, making the Rays the first club to clinch a postseason spot this year. The Milwaukee Brewers joined them a short time later. Drew Rasmussen drew a no-decision after seven strong innings, though the Rays won for the 10th consecutive time in games he has started. The AL West-leading Astros outhit the Rays 9-4. Yainer Diaz went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a walk. Brewers 20, Reds 0 Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in six runs, and Dustin May tossed six innings of two-hit ball as Milwaukee routed visiting Cincinnati to clinch its eighth postseason berth in nine seasons. The Brewers fell short of the biggest shutout in modern major league history, a record they tied on Aug. 18 by trouncing the Seattle Mariners 22-0. May (7-9) struck out six and walked one. Brice Turang (3-for-3, four RBIs) and Jake Bauers homered during a six-run second. The Brewers jumped on Andrew Abbott (6-11) for two runs in the first and six in the second, ending his outing after he allowed nine hits. Sal Stewart collected the only two hits for the Reds, who have lost four straight. Yankees 6, Mets 4 Carlos Rodon pitched 6 1/3 sharp innings and the host New York Yankees homered twice off rookie Nolan McLean in a victory over the New York Mets on the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. The Yankees won for the ninth time in 12 games while moving closer to clinching their ninth postseason spot in the past 10 seasons. Cody Bellinger hit a tiebreaking three-run homer off McLean (11-9) in the second and Ben Rice added a leadoff blast in the fifth. Rodon (6-3) allowed two runs, one earned, on three hits and finished with eight strikeouts. McLean allowed five runs and a career-high 10 hits in five innings. The Mets got a homer and an RBI single from rookie A.J. Ewing but had a four-game winning streak snapped. Braves 6, Phillies 5 (11 innings) Drake Baldwin lined a two-out RBI double to center field in the 11th to cap a two-run rally and lift Atlanta to a victory over visiting Philadelphia, giving the Braves some breathing room in the National League East. Atlanta, trailing 5-4, tied the game on Ha-Seong Kim's two-out single and walked it off on Baldwin's double against Brooks Raley (5-6). Didier Fuentes (7-2) was the winning pitcher. Philadelphia had taken the lead in the top of the 11th on an RBI single by Luis Arraez. The win allowed the Braves to extend their division lead over the Phillies to five games. Guardians 5, Twins 2 Angel Martinez went 2-for-4 with a two-run home run, and Cleveland scored three runs in the top of the ninth inning to secure a win over Minnesota in Minneapolis. Brayan Rocchio had a double and two RBIs for Cleveland in the opener of the three-game series. Travis Bazzana went 2-for-2 and scored twice for the Guardians, who hold a two-game lead over the Toronto Blue Jays for the American League's third and final wild-card spot. Royce Lewis and Kaelen Culpepper tallied one RBI apiece for Minnesota. Twins reliever Yoendrys Gomez (2-3) gave up three runs on two hits in one-third of an inning. Cardinals 7, White Sox 3 Rookie Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal each had three hits and drove in two runs for St. Louis in a victory against visiting Chicago. Alec Burleson had two hits and two RBIs for the Cardinals. Jordan Walker had two hits and two runs for St. Louis, which snapped a three-game losing streak. Chase Meidroth hit a pair of home runs for the White Sox, who lost their fourth straight game and had their AL Central lead trimmed to a half-game over the second-place Guardians. Randal Grichuk joined Meidroth in collecting two of Chicago's nine hits. Dodgers 6, Marlins 2 Kyle Tucker went 3-for-3 with a grand slam and a season-high five RBIs to lead visiting Los Angeles past Miami for its eighth straight win. Dodgers starter Blake Snell (4-1) struck out eight in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed one run on four hits. Max Muncy added three hits for Los Angeles, and Will Smith contributed an RBI single. Marlins starter Ryan Gusto (1-5) lasted six innings and held the Dodgers to two runs on five hits. Miami's offense was led by Otto Lopez, who went 4-for-5. Nationals 4, Angels 3 Jorbit Vivas hit a tiebreaking two-run double to cap a three-run eighth inning as host Washington snapped a seven-game losing streak with a comeback victory over Los Angeles. CJ Abrams had two hits and a run and James Wood had an RBI single and a walk for Washington. Clayton Beeter (6-5) tossed a scoreless eighth, and Erik Tolman earned his second save despite allowing a run. Mike Trout hit a home run and Christian Moore doubled and had two hits and two RBIs for the Angels, who finished with just four hits. Los Angeles reliever Samy Natera Jr. (1-2) allowed three runs on three hits in one inning. Padres 7, Giants 5 Dustin Harris and Freddy Fermin, the bottom two batters in the order, combined for four hits and four RBIs, Jackson Merrill chipped in with a double and two singles, and visiting San Diego overcame a Rafael Devers grand slam to beat San Francisco. Robbie Ray (12-8) threw five innings of five-run ball for the Padres, who maintained a half-game lead on the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third NL wild card. Mason Miller loaded the bases in the ninth but escaped for his 35th save. Giants starter Anthony Molina (3-1) allowed seven runs and nine hits in three innings. San Francisco's Jonah Cox had two hits and two runs. Diamondbacks 9, Rangers 1 Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado hit back-to-back homers in a five-run sixth inning, Ketel Marte doubled twice and drove in three runs, and Arizona topped Texas in Phoenix. Gabriel Moreno had two hits and two RBIs and Ildemaro Vargas had two hits and drove in a run for the D-backs, who posted their major-league-best 44th comeback victory and have won five of their past six. Reliever Kevin Ginkel (6-4) got two outs for the win. Joc Pederson had two of the Rangers' five hits, including an RBI double. MacKenzie Gore (8-11) was charged with four runs on five hits in four-plus innings. Cubs 12, Pirates 2 Alex Bregman belted a two-run homer and Michael Busch drove in three runs, fueling host Chicago to a victory over Pittsburgh. Chicago's Seiya Suzuki scored three runs and joined Bregman with three hits. Carson Kelly ripped a two-run double in the second inning for the Cubs, who banged out 16 hits en route to snapping a four-game losing streak. Pittsburgh rookie Konnor Griffin tripled to lead off the game and came around to score on an RBI single by Oneil Cruz. Bryan Reynolds capped a nine-pitch at-bat with a homer in the sixth inning for the Pirates, whose four-game winning streak ended. Royals 3, Red Sox 2 Kansas City scored three runs over the first three innings and let its pitching do the rest as the visitors held on to beat Boston. Carter Jensen had two doubles and an RBI and Salvador Perez went 2-for-4 with an RBI to lead the Royals. Seth Lugo (7-8) scattered seven hits and struck out seven across five innings of two-run ball. Steven Cruz registered his seventh save with a 1-2-3 ninth. Mickey Gasper homered and Wilyer Abreu went 2-for-4 with an RBI double for the Red Sox, who have lost three straight since a five-game winning streak. Sonny Gray (17-5) went six frames and allowed three runs on six hits. Orioles 7, Blue Jays 4 Dylan Beavers socked a solo home run and had three RBIs as visiting Baltimore defeated Toronto. Coby Mayo added a solo blast and Christian Encarnacion-Strand rapped out three hits for the Orioles, who have won three out of four. Chris Bassitt (7-5) tossed five-plus innings of two-run ball. Rico Garcia got the final out to earn his eighth save. Brett Bateman hit his first major league homer, a two-run shot, for the Blue Jays, and Kazuma Okamoto added a solo homer and a double. Max Scherzer (2-8) completed five innings, allowing six runs and seven hits. Tigers 6, Rockies 2 Dillon Dingler hit a two-run homer, Max Clark supplied a solo shot and Detroit pulled away to hand visiting Colorado its fifth straight loss. Riley Greene contributed a single, a double and a triple and two RBIs for the Tigers. Framber Valdez (10-10) held the Rockies to one unearned run and six hits in six innings. Kenley Jansen got the final out for his 19th save as Detroit won for the fourth time in six games. Colorado starter Mason Adams permitted one run and two hits in five innings. Mark Manfredi (1-2) gave up two runs while recording only two outs. Athletics 6, Mariners 5 (10 innings) Donovan Walton led off the bottom of the 10th inning with a two-run, walk-off homer to right as the Athletics recorded a dramatic victory over Seattle at West Sacramento, Calif. Walton jumped all over a 1-1 sweeper from Eduard Bazardo (3-4) for his third hit of the night to give the A's their seventh victory in nine games. Lawrence Butler had three hits, including a two-run homer, for the Athletics. Julio Rodriguez hit a run-scoring ground single with two outs in the top of the 10th to give Seattle a 5-4 lead prior to Walton's winning blast. Lazaro Montes delivered a pinch-hit, two-run blast for Seattle. --Field Level Media

item.title: China's Xi lands in Delhi for BRICS summit and talks with Modi
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in the Indian capital on Saturday for the summit of leaders of the BRICS group of countries and talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian TV channels showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in the Indian capital on Saturday for the summit of leaders of the BRICS group of countries and talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian TV channels showed. The visit is Xi's [USN:L4N44V073 TEXT:"first to India in seven years"] and comes as the Asian neighbours [USN:L6N4500OX TEXT:"cautiously rebuild ties"] that were badly damaged after a military clash on their disputed Himalayan border in 2020 in which 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed. Xi stepped out of his plane to a red carpet welcome and was greeted by women performing traditional Indian dances. The Xi-Modi meeting, scheduled for Saturday evening, will be their third in three years, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry said on Friday. China "is willing" to work together with India, to view two-way relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, properly manage differences, and be "good neighbours and friends, as well as mutually supportive partners," the spokesperson said. BRICS includes Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates. The summit is being held amid geopolitical tensions triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, the Russia-Ukraine war and the disruption they have caused to global energy, trade and transport.

item.title: Padres hold on to beat Giants, extend win streak to five
item.description: Dustin Harris and Freddy Fermin, the bottom two batters in the order, combined for four hits and four RBIs, Jackson Merrill chipped in with a double and two singles, and the visiting San Diego Padres overcame a Rafael Devers grand slam to beat the San Francisco Giants 7-5 in the opener of a three-game series Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dustin Harris and Freddy Fermin, the bottom two batters in the order, combined for four hits and four RBIs, Jackson Merrill chipped in with a double and two singles, and the visiting San Diego Padres overcame a Rafael Devers grand slam to beat the San Francisco Giants 7-5 in the opener of a three-game series Friday night. Robbie Ray (12-8) recorded a win in his return to San Francisco, helping the Padres (79-68) capture a fifth straight victory and remain a half-game ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks (79-69) in the duel for the final National League wild-card playoff spot. After the Giants opened the scoring on a Bryce Eldridge RBI single in the first inning, the Padres took the lead in the second when Harris singled in a run and Fermin doubled in another. San Diego appeared to break the game open with a five-run third in which Harris, with an RBI triple, and Fermin, with a run-scoring double, were involved again. Xander Bogaerts had the big hit of the uprising, a two-run double. Giants starter Anthony Molina (3-1) was pulled at inning's end, having allowed seven runs and nine hits in three innings. He walked two and struck out four. Yunior Marte kept the Giants in the game with five innings of shutout relief, allowing Devers' fifth-inning grand slam to get the hosts back in the game at 7-5. The homer was Devers' 36th of the year. Ray turned the ball over to the Padres bullpen after five innings, during which he was charged with five runs on four hits and four walks. He struck out five. Yuki Matsui, Adrian Morejon and Bradgley Rodriguez retained the two-run advantage with a scoreless inning of relief apiece, setting the stage in the ninth for Mason Miller, who loaded the bases with two outs before striking out Eldridge to secure his 35th save. Rodriguez's eighth inning included a leadoff double by Eldridge and two challenges by catcher Fermin that turned balls into strikeouts. Harris and Merrill scored twice apiece for the Padres, who collected five doubles and two triples among 12 hits. Eldridge and Jonah Cox, who scored twice, had two hits apiece for the Giants (62-86), who were coming off a three-game home sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals. --Field Level Media

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Austin Simmons, No. 23 Mizzou win Border War vs. Kansas

Donovan Olugbode and Cayden Lee finished with more than 100 yards receiving apiece and each caught a touchdown pass for Missouri (2-0), which won its fifth straight "Border War" matchup, a rivalry that began in 1891. Austin Alexander had an 88-yard touchdown return on a blocked field goal for Kansas (1-1), which has lost both meetings with Mizzou in a series that has been played only twice -- both in the past two seasons -- since the Tigers moved to the Southeastern Conference in 2012. Pribula completed 12 of 14 passes for 162 yards and one interception before sitting out the second half for Virginia (2-0).
