item.title: Explosion hits another EMCO weapons site in Bulgaria; probe underway
item.description: Bulgaria is investigating the cause of a fire at a weapons storage facility operated by EMCO, including the possibility of sabotage and a link to a previous blaze at another of the company's facilities in August, the interior minister said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bulgaria is investigating the cause of a fire at a weapons storage facility operated by EMCO, including the possibility of sabotage and a link to a previous blaze at another of the company's facilities in August, the interior minister said. No injuries were reported in the fire, which broke out near the village of Tsareva Livada and lit up the night sky, according to videos broadcast locally. The incident came weeks after an explosion and fire at another EMCO weapons depot in western Bulgaria. Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev told journalists on Saturday that the fire was under control and that an investigation was underway. "We will review previous cases in which similar fires occurred in the warehouses of this company, as well as at other companies, in order to look for a possible connection or a similar pattern," he said. "We are not ruling out outside interference." EMCO is run by Bulgarian arms trader Emilian Gebrev, who Bulgarian prosecutors have previously alleged was the target of attacks on his facilities by Russian operatives. In 2024, Bulgaria issued arrest warrants for six Russian citizens accused of involvement in the destruction of EMCO arms depots that stored munitions destined for export to Ukraine and Georgia between 2011 and 2020. Prosecutors at the time said they had grounds to suspect links between the blasts in Bulgaria, an attempted poisoning of Gebrev in 2015, and munitions depot explosions in the Czech Republic in 2014. Moscow has dismissed the allegations. Slavcho Dimiev, manager of EMCO's production facilities, confirmed Saturday's fire at the storage site, which he said mainly holds ammunition, including a small quantity of medium-calibre rounds. He told reporters that additional measures should be considered to protect such facilities. "If it is ultimately concluded that they have been targeted, this is not an attack on a particular company alone; it is an attack on the national interest," he said.

item.title: Pachuca golea como visitante al Atlante en torneo mexicano
item.description: Pachuca goleó el viernes como visitante al Atlante por 3-0 en el inicio de la octava jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pachuca goleó el viernes como visitante al Atlante por 3-0 en el inicio de la octava jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. Con su tercer triunfo en el torneo, los "Tuzos" de Pachuca llegaron a 11 puntos para subir del duodécimo al noveno lugar general. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, Pachuca se adelantó a los 13 minutos con un disparo del venezolano Salomón Rondón que fue desviado por un zaguero del Atlante y dejó sin oportunidad de reaccionar al portero Óscar Jiménez. Pachuca aumentó su ventaja a los 20 minutos cuando el brasileño Robert Kenedy metió el balón por el ángulo derecho con un zurdazo en la entrada del área. El tercer gol del equipo visitante cayó a los 37 minutos con un potente disparo del neerlandés Oussama Idrissi con el que el balón pegó en el travesaño antes de que cayera dentro de la portería. En los otros encuentros del viernes, Puebla venció por 1-0 como visitante a Necaxa con un gol del uruguayo Mathías Tomas, quien metió el balón por el ángulo derecho con un potente zurdazo desde fuera del área a los 93 minutos. En tanto, Querétaro ganó por 1-0 en su visita a Tijuana con gol del argentino Mateo Coronel. La jornada continuará el sábado con los partidos entre Toluca-Atlas, Monterrey-Tigres UANL y Cruz Azul-América. El domingo, Guadalajara enfrentará a Pumas UNAM, mientras que Santos Laguna jugará ante Bravos de Ciudad Juárez. La jornada se completará el lunes cuando León sea local ante el Atlético de San Luis.

item.title: Shelton relishing challenge of first Grand Slam final against Zverev
item.description: Ben Shelton said he was thriving in unfamiliar territory after reaching his first Grand Slam final at the U.S. Open, with the American crediting a newfound consistency for his breakthrough run in New York.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Ben Shelton said he was thriving in unfamiliar territory after reaching his first Grand Slam final at the U.S. Open, with the American crediting a newfound consistency for his breakthrough run in New York. Shelton beat compatriot Frances Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 on Friday to book a final with German top seed Alexander Zverev and move closer to ending a 23-year American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam champion since Andy Roddick's triumph in New York. The 23-year-old will also aim to become the first Black American man to capture the New York title since Arthur Ashe in 1968, but knows he must earn a first victory over Zverev in their sixth meeting. "This whole tournament at this point has been unchartered territory," Shelton told reporters. "I'm in positions I've never been in before. I've beaten guys that I've never beaten before. I'm just excited to put it all out on the line. "I can think about how cool this moment is and what I'm playing for. At the end of the day, I'm here in New York, I'm hanging out with my team, I'm with my homies playing a little bit of tennis and I've been able to downplay the moment well. "I've got great people around me that keep me grounded and focused and humble, and I think these moments I want to cherish, I don't want to take lightly. But at the same time, it's very business-like the way I've been going about it." While Shelton acknowledged the nerves that come with the biggest match of his career, he said the chance to test himself against the top seed on the sport's grandest stages on Sunday was something he was embracing. "The nerves are always there," he added. "It's something that you've got to lean into. The nerves are as much there in the first round for me as in the semis, and I'm sure the finals will be the same. "It's something you've got to be able to overcome, but I'm having fun, you know? I'm playing against the number one seed, playing against a Grand Slam champion trying to get my first. "It's a lot of reasons that this is an enjoyable moment for me. Knowing I can leave it all on court and push myself to the absolute limit ... and see what I can do is an exciting thought."

item.title: Spurs' Mudryk sidelined by injury after comeback from doping ban
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhailo Mudryk injured his ankle in training, according to British media reports, with manager Roberto De Zerbi hoping the Ukraine international can return as soon as possible after this latest setback.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhailo Mudryk injured his ankle in training, according to British media reports, with manager Roberto De Zerbi hoping the Ukraine international can return as soon as possible after this latest setback. The 25-year-old [USN:L1N44T14D TEXT:"joined Spurs on a season-long loan"] from rivals Chelsea on transfer deadline day and made his debut off the bench in last weekend's goalless [USN:L1N44X04B TEXT:"draw at Nottingham Forest"]. Mudryk is expected to be sidelined until after the international break, said the media reports. Mudryk previously played under De Zerbi on Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk before joining Chelsea in January 2023. He struggled to establish himself at Stamford Bridge, however, and his career was put on hold after an adverse analytical finding for meldonium in an anti-doping test in 2024. The Football Association handed him a four-year ban, but he appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and his [USN:L6N43X13J TEXT:"suspension was later reduced"] following an agreement between the FA and the World Anti-Doping Agency. "(With) Mudryk, it was a stupid injury and we hope he can come back as soon as possible. For him and for us," De Zerbi told reporters on Friday. "For him because he suffered too much and for us because we lost an important player. "He played 15 minutes in Nottingham, he played well, but it's in the normal process when one player doesn't play for a long time." Mudryk made 73 appearances for Chelsea, scoring 10 goals and registering 11 assists before his move to Spurs. Spurs have made a disappointing start to the season, taking just one point from their opening three Premier League matches to sit 17th in the table. They host Everton later on Saturday.

item.title: Syrian private airport plans spark outcry over mass graves, land rights
item.description: Syrian government plans to turn a former military airport in Damascus into a hub for private jets are raising alarm among rights groups and residents who say redevelopment could disturb suspected mass graves and override private land claims.
item.dc:creator: Feras Dalatey
item.content:encoded: Syrian government plans to turn a former military airport in Damascus into a hub for private jets are raising alarm among rights groups and residents who say redevelopment could disturb suspected mass graves and override private land claims. Syria’s civil aviation authority said last week it was preparing to reclassify Mezzeh military airport for limited civilian use, focused on private and executive aviation, to complement Damascus International Airport, according to a report on Syria's state news agency, SANA. Rubble removal and infrastructure upgrades had already begun, the report said. The project is emerging as a test of how Syria’s new authorities balance a [USN:L1N44L0PT TEXT:"drive to attract investment"] and redevelop state assets with two unresolved legacies of Assad’s family rule: the fate of tens of thousands of missing Syrians and property rights clouded by decades of expropriation. NEW DOCUMENTS SHOW AIRPORT'S ROLE AS EXECUTION SITE Under ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad and his father Hafez, Mezzeh housed key branches of the powerful Air Force Intelligence Directorate, as well as numerous detention facilities where suspected government opponents were tortured, executed and subjected to enforced disappearance. Parts of the air base were used for presidential and other official flights. Air Force Intelligence (AFI) documents recently obtained by the Syria Justice and Accountability Centre (SJAC), a U.S.-based Syrian-led human rights group, and shared exclusively with Reuters, show that senior Syrian military officials approved Mezzeh in 2012 as a site for carrying out executions of detainees sentenced to death by military field courts. One document proposed moving executions from [USN:L8N3NA0UJ TEXT:"Sednaya"] — the country's most notorious prison at the time — to Mezzeh because it was a "closed security compound" close to Damascus. Subsequent correspondence discussed a firing range and later a hangar beside the runway as execution sites. The documents, which underscore the central role of Mezzeh in the Assad-era security system, show officials ordered construction of a platform at the hangar, requested nylon rope and directed that the work be carried out under AFI supervision “in utmost secrecy.” A 2025 [USN:L6N3PH0O2 TEXT:"investigation"] by SJAC identified two suspected grave sites linked to people who died in detention at Mezzeh, where it said more than 1,150 detainees died, some by execution and others from torture or maltreatment. In a July 2025 letter seen by Reuters, SJAC provided Syria’s National Commission for Missing Persons with the coordinates of the two suspected graves inside the airport, urging authorities to prevent construction or excavation until the sites were investigated. The commission told SJAC at the time that there were no construction or refurbishment plans for Mezzeh, SJAC told Reuters. SJAC wrote to the commission again on September 8 after the redevelopment plans emerged, warning that excavation, rubble removal or other works could damage human remains and evidence crucial to identifying victims, according to a second letter seen by Reuters. SJAC told Reuters it had not yet received a response to its second letter. Amer Matar, founder of the Syria Prisons Museum, a Germany-based NGO documenting detention facilities including those at Mezzeh, said the planned works showed a lack of respect for Syrian families who still have no answers on the fate of loved ones detained under Assad. "To construct a business airport on a site that may contain mass graves, without a thorough prior investigation, without site protection, without searching for the missing and their remains, and without preserving evidence, is an act of extreme recklessness and disregard," Matar told Reuters. The Syrian civil aviation authority, Syria's National Commission for Missing Persons and Syria's defense ministry, which has been operating the airport, did not respond to questions from Reuters about suspected graves and land claims. SANA cited the civil aviation authority's spokesperson as saying that Mezzeh's refurbishment would take into account the surrounding urban area and relevant legal and social issues, but did not specifically mention the graves or land rights. It is unclear who will develop the airport. RESIDENTS PROTEST OVER LAND CLAIMS The dispute over the land on which airport facilities were built is decades old. Under the Assads, private land was regularly expropriated for government projects, often without compensation. Mezzeh airport was built on land belonging to hundreds of private citizens across 2.76 sq km (1.1 square miles), according to land records from the Moadamiya municipality shared with Reuters. A former municipal official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters that expropriation decrees retroactively justified the government's use of those lands when the airport was built in 1956, and that compensation had not been paid. Residents demonstrated in Moadamiya a day after the redevelopment plans were announced. “We welcome investment, but we should be sitting at the table and discussing our share with investors, not the state,” said one protest organiser, who gave his name as Abu Khaled. “We have a documented right to this land.” The dispute comes as Syria faces calls to address Assad-era property seizures. On September 2, United Nations land rights experts appealed to Syria's government to suspend and repeal laws they said had enabled systematic property dispossession under Assad, and to either establish mechanisms to return properties to their legitimate owners, or provide adequate compensation.

item.title: Trump says he would 'love' to see a united Ireland
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would "love" to see British-run Northern Ireland unify with Ireland, remarks made during a visit to Dublin that drew a sharp response from pro-British unionists in Northern Ireland.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Padraic Halpin, Conor Humphries
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would "love" to see British-run Northern Ireland unify with Ireland, remarks made during a visit to Dublin that drew a sharp response from pro-British unionists in Northern Ireland. Trump's comments come weeks after new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said a referendum on Northern Ireland leaving the United Kingdom was "off the table", a position Downing Street on Saturday [USN:S8N443004 TEXT:"said remained unchanged"]. "Well, I don't want to cause any problems, but I will tell you, I'd love to see it unified," Trump told reporters sitting next to Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin after the pair met in Dublin. "It's going to happen eventually ... I think it would be a fantastic thing." 'A VERY COOL THING' "Now the UK will have something to say about it ... but I think it would be a great thing," he added. Trump later said that there "was no good answer" to the question on Irish unity but repeated that he thought it would be "a very cool thing". Under the terms of the 1998 Good Friday Agreement, a referendum on Northern Ireland leaving the UK can be held only at the discretion of the British government. The accord ended three decades of violence between Irish nationalists seeking a united Ireland and unionists who wanted Northern Ireland to remain part of the UK. While polls show a comfortable majority in Northern Ireland favour remaining in the UK, the gap has narrowed slightly since Britain's departure from the European Union pushed unity higher up the political agenda. The leader of Northern Ireland's largest unionist party, the Democratic Unionist Party, rejected Trump's prediction, saying unification would lead to "the destruction of our country." "Northern Ireland's constitutional future will be decided by the people of Northern Ireland, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington," Gavin Robinson, who has publicly supported Trump in the past, wrote on X. Previous U.S. presidents, including those with strong Irish heritage like Joe Biden, have been careful to remain neutral on Irish unification. The U.S. government played a key role in brokering the 1998 peace deal. 'YOU FLEECED US' Trump is making the 48-hour trip as his Republican Party campaigns to retain its majorities in both chambers of the U.S. Congress. He is due to attend a golf tournament at one of his resorts later on Saturday. Trump also met Irish President Catherine Connolly, who was [USN:L8N3W10ZL TEXT:"elected"] head of state last year. When Trump last visited Ireland as president in 2019, Connolly, an outspoken politician with [USN:L8N3W50JH TEXT:"far-left"] foreign policy views, protested outside Shannon Airport in western Ireland. Anti-war and anti-Trump protests are planned in Dublin on Saturday and in western Ireland near the Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg. Martin focused his remarks on the countries' close economic ties. U.S.-owned companies, mainly in the technology and pharmaceutical sectors, employ about 10% of workers in Ireland after successive governments [USN:L8N41412H TEXT:"prioritized"] their jobs and tax dollars over decades. "You took all our medical companies, we've got to get a couple of them back," Trump said. "You fleeced us but that's okay... There's a lot of room to go around and our relationship with you is fantastic."

item.title: Back-to-back big innings propel Diamondbacks past Rangers
item.description: Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado hit back-to-back homers in a five-run sixth inning, Ketel Marte doubled twice and drove in three runs and the Arizona Diamondbacks stopped the Texas Rangers 9-1 on Friday in Phoenix.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado hit back-to-back homers in a five-run sixth inning, Ketel Marte doubled twice and drove in three runs and the Arizona Diamondbacks stopped the Texas Rangers 9-1 on Friday in Phoenix. Gabriel Moreno had two hits and two RBIs and Ildemaro Vargas had two hits and drove in a run for the D-backs, who posted their major-league-best 44th comeback victory and have won five of their past six. Carroll hit a two-run homer and Arenado followed in the sixth after Arizona knocked out Texas starter MacKenzie Gore (8-11) amid producing four runs and four doubles in the fifth. Carroll, who missed the previous two games with lower back discomfort, broke a 5-for-48 slump with his 20th homer. Arenado hit his 24th. Joc Pederson had two of Texas' five hits, with his RBI double giving the Rangers a 1-0 lead in the fifth off starter Merrill Kelly. Arizona's Kevin Ginkel (6-4) entered and got Brandon Nimmo to ground out with the bases loaded to end the inning. Four Arizona relievers gave up three hits in 4 2/3 scoreless innings. Justin Martinez struck out the side on nine pitches in the sixth, the fifth immaculate inning in franchise history. The D-backs (79-69) remained a half-game behind the San Diego Padres (79-68) for the final National League wild-card spot. Those two clubs are within striking distance of the NL wild-card leaders, the Philadelphia Phillies and Chicago Cubs (both 82-66). The Rangers (72-76), who have lost five of seven, remained three games behind Houston (75-73) for the American League West lead and fell three games behind the Cleveland Guardians (75-73) for the final AL wild-card spot. Arizona's Jordan Lawlar led off the fifth with a double. Ryan Waldschmidt walked, and Vargas doubled to tie the game. Marte followed with a two-run double for a 3-1 lead, chasing Gore. Facing Jakob Junis, Moreno singled in Marte. Marte doubled home Waldschmidt in the sixth, and Moreno singled in Marte before Carroll's two-run homer and Arenado's shot capped the five-run inning. Kelly gave up two hits and one run in 4 1/3 innings, with three walks and three strikeouts. Gore was charged with four runs on five hits in four-plus innings, with two strikeouts and three walks. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tiafoe proud of comeback season despite Shelton semi-final loss
item.description: Frances Tiafoe said learning to close out matches will be his next challenge after falling to compatriot Ben Shelton in the U.S. Open semi-finals on Friday, but the 11th seed left New York proud of a season that will lift him back into the world's top 10.
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Frances Tiafoe said learning to close out matches will be his next challenge after falling to compatriot Ben Shelton in the U.S. Open semi-finals on Friday, but the 11th seed left New York proud of a season that will lift him back into the world's top 10. Tiafoe, appearing in his third U.S. Open semi-final, was unable to take the final step, falling to eighth seed [USN:L1N45401J TEXT:"Shelton 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5."] Yet his run at Flushing Meadows guaranteed the 28-year-old will climb to a new career-high ranking of world number eight once the post-tournament rankings are released, returning him to the top 10 for the first time since 2023. "It's been a great season for me, but also, you know, this one is tough," Tiafoe told reporters. "We wanted to win this one. You know, it's just the last couple of weeks, it's been great weeks, but haven't been able to finish, and that's probably going to be the next thing for me. "I was doing my interview here last year, and it was really bad how I felt where I was at," he said. "I'm upset, but I'm at the same time so proud of myself of where I've been." Tiafoe said his ultimate goal, winning a major title, remained unchanged. "I want to do the thing, man. I want to be a Grand Slam champion one day and just get back to the drawing board and keep working," he said. The support he receives in New York made another deep run particularly meaningful, but also left him wanting more. "I just want to win it, man. I mean, the love is incredible. It's something that gives me definitely tears in my eyes from a kid starting how I did, and the love I have here is crazy." He will now turn his attention to the final stretch of the season and a place at the ATP Finals in Turin, November's season-ending event for the highest-ranked players. "I'm going to probably feel sorry for myself the next couple of days, but after that, I can start working again and get to Turin," he said.

item.title: Rookies power Cardinals to win as White Sox's division lead shrinks
item.description: Rookie Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal each had three hits and drove in two runs Friday night for the St. Louis Cardinals in a 7-3 victory against the visiting Chicago White Sox.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Joshua Baez and Leo Bernal each had three hits and drove in two runs Friday night for the St. Louis Cardinals in a 7-3 victory against the visiting Chicago White Sox. Alec Burleson had two hits and two RBIs for the Cardinals, whose own hopes remain dim in the National League wild-card race. The Cardinals (73-75) did manage to strike a blow against the first-place White Sox's chances of winning the American League Central. Chase Meidroth hit a pair of home runs for Chicago, which had its division lead trimmed to a half-game over the second-place Cleveland Guardians (75-73), who beat the Minnesota Twins 5-2 on Friday. The White Sox (75-72) lost their fourth straight game. Baez hit an RBI single against Anthony Kay to break a 2-2 tie in the third inning after Meidroth went deep in each of his first two at-bats against Matthew Liberatore. Meidroth has 14 home runs on the season. The Cardinals added three runs in the fifth, with Burleson hitting an RBI single, Baez an RBI double and Bernal an RBI single for a 6-2 lead. Bernal also brought in Baez with a seventh-inning single. Gordon Graceffo (8-1) entered in the fifth to get two outs in relief of Liberatore, who allowed two runs, six hits and three walks over 4 1/3 innings. Liberatore struck out two. Kay (9-9) allowed three runs, five hits and a walk while fanning two over four innings. Trevor Richards gave up three runs in two innings. Jordan Walker had two hits and two runs for St. Louis, which snapped a three-game losing streak. Closer Riley O'Brien pitched a 1-2-3 ninth inning in a non-save situation. Randal Gricuk joined Meidroth in collecting two of Chicago's nine hits. Colson Montgomery went 0-for-4 with three strikeouts and a walk. The White Sox have scored a combined eight runs in their losing streak, which began with a three-game sweep at the hands of the Pittsburgh Pirates. item.title: Antonio returns to English football with Watford move
item.description: Watford have signed Michail Antonio on a free transfer on a one-year deal, bringing the former West Ham United forward back to English football.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Watford have signed Michail Antonio on a free transfer on a one-year deal, bringing the former West Ham United forward back to English football. The 36-year-old, West Ham's all-time leading Premier League goalscorer, was in a serious road accident in December 2024 when his car hit a tree on the way home from training. He broke his thigh bone in four places and did not play for the club again. Antonio left West Ham in August 2025 after the London club opted not to renew his contract. They were relegated to the second-tier Championship after finishing 18th in the Premier League the last season. He joined Qatari side Al-Sailiya in March, his first club since undergoing surgery following the accident. "It's a good set of boys here," Antonio said in a statement on Friday. "They are focused and ready to show their abilities this season. "Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can. "I've scored a few goals against Watford! So hopefully I can score some for Watford now when I'm fully up to speed." Watford are 12th in the Championship with eight points from six matches.

item.title: Trump criticizes Smithsonian's focus on oppression
item.description: President Donald Trump criticized what he called the Smithsonian's overwhelming focus on oppression on Friday and called for a five-year exhibition on George Washington, in his latest critique of an institution he has repeatedly attacked.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump criticized what he called the Smithsonian's overwhelming focus on oppression on Friday and called for a five-year exhibition on George Washington, in his latest critique of an institution he has repeatedly attacked. The Republican leader has [USN:L4N43B04S TEXT:"denounced"] the Smithsonian for months, in what critics call part of a campaign to present U.S. history from a conservative point of view. On Tuesday, Smithsonian chief [USN:L6N4500XX TEXT:"Lonnie Bunch"] said he was retiring. Trump said on Truth Social that "under recently ended leadership," the Smithsonian took steps "to focus attention overwhelmingly on those who have been oppressed, but there is almost no attention paid to those who triumphed over great oppression, and against great odds." "I am calling on the Smithsonian Institution to honor the Life and Legacy of George Washington, America's Greatest Hero, with a five-year exhibition at the National Museum of American History, beginning now, and continuing through, February 22, 2032, the 300th anniversary of Washington's birth," Trump added. Trump said he was also calling on the Smithsonian to "erect a 30-foot (9-m) 'Colossus statue'" of Washington outside the museum. He also asked the Smithsonian to install an 11-foot (3.4-m)statue of Washington that was featured at the recent Freedom 250 Grand Prix race in the museum's Flag Hall. The Trump administration has [USN:L1N44V03S TEXT:"previously threatened"] to cut federal funding and federal agencies' support for the Smithsonian, with Trump expressing displeasure at what he called the institution's excessive focus on how bad slavery was. Last year, his administration [USN:L1N3U415T TEXT:"launched a review"] of some museums and his White House has accused the institution's National Museum of American History of "[USN:L4N43B04S TEXT:"thinly veiled anti-Americanism"]." Trump has also ordered installation of signs outside the museum to reflect his administration's criticism. Historians and civil rights advocates have denounced Trump's attacks and his accusations against the institution, saying such steps risk reversing social progress and undermine the acknowledgement of critical phases of U.S. history. Trump says he aims to remove "anti-American ideology." Bunch has said the White House's accusations against the National Museum of American History were unfair. The Smithsonian is a vast museum and research complex and a premier exhibition space for U.S. history and culture, with 21 museums and galleries and the National Zoo. Trump has [USN:L4N3YU0BK TEXT:"targeted"] U.S. cultural and historical institutions - from museums to monuments to national parks - with his declarations and orders leading to the dismantling of slavery exhibits and the restoration of Confederate statues.

item.title: Braves edge Phillies in 11-inning thriller, increase NL East lead
item.description: Drake Baldwin lined a two-out RBI double to center field in the 11th inning to cap a two-run rally and give the Atlanta Braves a 6-5 victory over the visiting Philadelphia Phillies on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drake Baldwin lined a two-out RBI double to center field in the 11th inning to cap a two-run rally and give the Atlanta Braves a 6-5 victory over the visiting Philadelphia Phillies on Friday. Atlanta, trailing 5-4, tied the game on Ha-Seong Kim's two-out single and walked it off on Baldwin's double against Brooks Raley (5-6). Didier Fuentes (7-2) was the winning pitcher. Philadelphia had taken the lead in the top of the 11th on an RBI single by Luis Arraez. The win allowed the Braves (87-61) to extend their National League East lead over the Phillies (82-66) to five games. Neither starting pitcher figured in the decision. Atlanta's Chris Sale allowed three runs -- all in the second inning -- on three hits and two walks with six strikeouts in seven innings. Philadelphia's Aaron Nola gave up two runs in 6 1/3 innings. He allowed six hits and three walks, striking out three. Matt Olson gave the Braves a 1-0 lead in the first with an opposite-field homer, his 38th, that clipped the left field foul pole. It was his first home run since Aug. 26 against the Dodgers. Derek Hill produced Philadelphia's offense in the second. With two outs, Edmundo Sosa singled, Bryan De La Cruz walked and J.T. Realmuto was hit by a pitch. With the bases loaded, Hill split the gap with a double that cleared the bases for a 3-1 lead. Atlanta cut its deficit to 3-2 when Austin Riley led off the seventh with a 434-foot homer into the left-center-field stands. The Braves tied the game in the ninth against Jonathan Bowlan. Mike Yastrzemski, who was 3-for-3, singled with one out. Pinch runner DaShawn Keirsey Jr. scored when Sean Murphy singled and center fielder Hill bobbled the ball for an error. Both teams scored in the 10th. The Phillies scored when Justin Crawford lined the first pitch from Raisel Iglesias to center field to drive in automatic runner Bryson Stott. Atlanta tied it when automatic runner Brewer Hicklen, who pinch ran for Olson, scored on Mauricio Dubon's sacrifice fly to center. The game's first pitch was delayed 47 minutes after a thunderstorm swept through the area. --Field Level Media

item.title: Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk acquitted in murder-for-hire trial
item.description: Grammy-winning rap artist Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: Grammy-winning rap artist Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago. Two co-defendants tried with the recording artist, whose real name is Durk Banks, were acquitted of murder-for-hire-related charges but were found guilty on charges of conspiracy to commit stalking, as well as stalking with a dangerous weapon and stalking resulting death. Although Banks was found not guilty of all those charges, he remains in custody and faces a separate trial scheduled for October 5 on murder-related racketeering and weapons offenses, according to a spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Los Angeles. His two co-defendants, Deandre Dontrell Wilson and David Brian Lindsey, face trial on the same counts. According to a 32-page federal indictment filed in the case, Banks is the ringleader of a violent criminal gang consisting of associates from his rap music label, One of the Family, that has engaged in robbery, murder and drug trafficking. The trial that ended on Friday stemmed from a fatal shooting on August 2022 at a gasoline station near the Beverly Center shopping mall in Los Angeles that prosecutors described as a planned hit. Banks, 33, who won the 2024 Grammy for best melodic rap performance for his hit single "All My Life," was accused of ordering, financing and masterminding the intended murder of a rival rapper Quando Rondo, born Tyquian Bowman. According to prosecutors, Banks placed a bounty on Bowman's head as revenge for the killing two years earlier of a close friend of Banks, Dayvon "King Von" Bennett, by one of Bowman's associates in an Atlanta nightclub. But the squad of killers who Banks allegedly sent to hunt down Bowman ended up killing Bowman's 24-year-old cousin, Saviay'a Robinson, by mistake, in a hail of gunfire. Banks, who was arrested in October 2024 at a Florida airport after five other suspects were charged in the case, has pleaded not guilty to all charges. Defense lawyers have asserted that Banks had nothing to do with the plot, maintaining that it was a former personal assistant who ordered the hit to impress his boss, the Los Angeles City News Service reported in its account of the trial. The ex-assistant and two other Banks associates originally indicted with the rapper reached plea deals in the case and testified for the prosecution, according to CNS. Banks' acquittal set off a celebration by the rap artist's supporters outside the downtown Los Angeles federal courthouse where the trial was held.

item.title: Guardians boost playoff hopes with 3-run ninth vs. Twins
item.description: Angel Martinez went 2-for-4 with a two-run home run, and the Cleveland Guardians scored three runs in the top of the ninth inning to secure a 5-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Friday night in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Angel Martinez went 2-for-4 with a two-run home run, and the Cleveland Guardians scored three runs in the top of the ninth inning to secure a 5-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Friday night in Minneapolis. Brayan Rocchio finished 1-for-3 with a double and two RBIs for Cleveland (75-73) in the opener of the three-game series. Travis Bazzana went 2-for-2 and scored twice for the Guardians, who hold a two-game lead over the Toronto Blue Jays for the American League's third and final wild-card spot. Royce Lewis and Kaelen Culpepper tallied one RBI apiece for Minnesota (69-78), which trails Cleveland by 5 1/2 games for the final AL wild-card spot. Guardians reliever Hunter Gaddis (4-3) pitched 1 1/3 innings of scoreless relief. Twins reliever Yoendrys Gomez (2-3) gave up three runs on two hits in one-third of an inning. Cade Smith earned his 36th save for the Guardians with a scoreless ninth. The score was 2-all when Cleveland broke through in the ninth. Bazzana walked, moved to third on Martinez's double and scored the go-ahead run on a wild pitch by Gomez. Rocchio increased the lead to 5-2 moments later with a two-run double to center. The Twins opened the scoring in the second. Kody Clemens hit a one-out single to center, and Lewis delivered in the next at-bat with an RBI double to left. The sequence marked Lewis' 52nd RBI of the season, matching a career high that he set in 2023 and equaled in 2025. Twins starter Taj Bradley delivered a strong performance with six scoreless innings, but the Guardians wasted no time taking advantage of the bullpen in the top of the seventh. Bazzana led off the inning with a hard-hit single to center. Martinez stepped to the plate two batters later, swung at a low first-pitch fastball and crushed a two-run homer 445 feet over the wall in left-center field. The monster blast gave the Guardians a 2-1 lead and marked the 15th home run of the season for Martinez. Minnesota evened the score in the bottom of the seventh. Culpepper lifted a two-out single just above a leaping Jose Ramirez at third base, and Austin Martin sprinted from second base to score with a headfirst slide. --Field Level Media

item.title: Shelton advances to US Open final for Zverev showdown
item.description: Ben Shelton defeated compatriot Frances Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 in an electric U.S. Open semi-final on Friday to secure a title clash with Alexander Zverev and move closer to ending a 23-year American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam champion.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Ben Shelton defeated compatriot Frances Tiafoe 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5 in an electric U.S. Open semi-final on Friday to secure a title clash with Alexander Zverev and move closer to ending a 23-year American wait for a men's singles Grand Slam champion. Zverev [USN:L1N4530XD TEXT:"booked his place"] in Sunday's final by fighting past unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov 6-3 7-6(7) 7-6(6) earlier in the day to close in on a second major title. Victory sent the German top seed into his second final in New York after his runner-up finish in 2020 to Dominic Thiem. Shelton, the big-hitting 23-year-old, now stands one victory away from becoming the first American man to win a major singles title since Andy Roddick hoisted the trophy at Flushing Meadows in 2003. With the semi-final line-up having already ensured a Black American man would reach the final, Shelton's win made him the first to do so in New York since Arthur Ashe in 1972, and at any of the majors since MaliVai Washington at Wimbledon in 1996. French Open champion Zverev was [USN:L1N4530YC TEXT:"pushed to five sets"] in each of his opening two rounds, but has now won four straight matches without dropping a set to charge into his third consecutive major final and stand in Shelton's path. "I'm going for it," Shelton said. "I'm going to leave it all on the court. I hope you guys come and back me, let's do this for the U.S. "It's a lot of emotion. My dad, my mom have sacrificed a lot for me to be in this position today. My dad lost his mom earlier this year and she's the reason he was able to play tennis. "Without her there's no Ben Shelton standing here today. This one is for her." POIGNANT START TO EVENING On a poignant evening that began with commemorations marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, Tiafoe powered ahead 5-4 when Shelton produced a double fault, before raising the roof on the main showcourt with a hold to bag the first set. "It's a difficult day to be out here playing," Shelton said. "My thoughts and prayers are going out to all the families who are impacted by 9/11. This is one of the greatest cities in the world and one of the biggest tragedies. But yeah, thoughts and prayers to everyone involved and affected." Tiafoe continued to target his opponent's relatively weaker backhand in the second set but Shelton dialled up the intensity to draw level and broke in the fifth game of the third set to take a commanding lead. With his booming left-handed serve and his defence proving impenetrable in the high-octane fourth set, eighth seed Shelton heaped the pressure on late and moved into his maiden major final after a double fault by Tiafoe. "Frances, he's like a big brother to me," Shelton added. "Every time we get to take this court together, Arthur Ashe Stadium, and play each other is super special. But this is where we want to be at the tail end ... this is our favourite tournament, our favourite court in the world. "To be able to light it up in front of you guys is the best feeling there is." Top seeds Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend earlier secured a [USN:L6N45316D TEXT:"team career Grand Slam"] with a 5-7 6-0 6-2 victory over American wildcards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery in the women's doubles final. The action will resume on Saturday when defending champion Aryna Sabalenka of Belarus faces incoming world number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan in the [USN:L4N45319U TEXT:"women's singles final"].

item.title: King Oyo, once world's youngest monarch, to be buried in western Uganda
item.description: Uganda's Tooro Kingdom prepared on Saturday to bury its late king, Oyo Nyimba, long the world's youngest monarch, following days of a bitter succession battle within the royal family.
item.dc:creator: Elias Biryabarema
item.content:encoded: Uganda's Tooro Kingdom prepared on Saturday to bury its late king, Oyo Nyimba, long the world's youngest monarch, following days of a [USN:L6N4520G9 TEXT:"bitter succession battle"] within the royal family. Royal guards clad in orange shawls and beating wooden sticks led the hearse carrying Oyo's casket in a solemn procession through the streets of the kingdom's capital, Fort Portal, in western Uganda. King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV made global headlines in 1995 when he took the throne at age 3. Images of the toddler king donning a crown and royal robes sparked curiosity and adoration around the world. He [USN:L1N44P087 TEXT:"died"] last month at 34 in the United States, where he was receiving treatment for cancer. His casket, draped in the blue-and-yellow Tooro flag, was driven from the royal palace to St. John's Cathedral for a ceremony before hundreds of mourners, including senior Ugandan government officials and delegations from chiefdoms in neighbouring countries. Uganda is led by an elected head of state but retains several kingdoms that pre-date the British colonial era and are seen as bulwarks of traditional identity and heritage. Oyo went on to become a U.N. goodwill ambassador who championed the fight against HIV and AIDS. "Although he became king and carried responsibilities far beyond what most people ever experience, he never completely lost the young boy who loved to have fun," said his sister, Ruth Komuntale, in her eulogy. SUCCESSION BATTLE THREATENED TO DELAY BURIAL After the cathedral service, Oyo will be buried at the site of the royal tombs. The Omusuna, the traditional chief priest charged with burying Tooro's monarchs, will guide the incoming king in the custom of casting nine coffee berries into the grave. Whether the new king would be in place to perform that mandatory rite had been in doubt. A committee consisting of members of the royal clan announced on Wednesday it had [USN:L8N45123S TEXT:"chosen Oyo's cousin"], Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a news anchor and editor at state broadcaster UBC, as king. But Oyo's immediate family said his hitherto unknown son should succeed him, as called for in the late king's will. Oyo never married and was not known to have any children until the kingdom's prime minister said he had a son in the August 27 statement announcing his death. Supporters of Kijanangoma's succession say Oyo's family has not been able to produce basic information about the purported son. A source with knowledge of crisis talks over the matter said Ugandan authorities had successfully pushed through Kijanangoma's succession on Friday. A government spokesperson could not be reached for comment. The Archbishop of the Church of Uganda, Stephen Kazimba Mugalu, called for unity within the royal family. "Words spoken in grief can cause pain, division and conflict," he told mourners. "It can even destroy the legacy of the king we are mourning." LATE KING WAS CHAMPION OF FIGHT AGAINST HIV, FRIEND OF GADDAFI Oyo himself took the throne after a protracted succession battle that finished in court. In addition to his ceremonial responsibilities and campaigning against HIV and AIDS, Oyo cultivated close ties with former Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, whom he named a special adviser to the monarch. Gaddafi donated money towards refurbishment of the royal palace. The 56-year-old Kijanangoma, who maintained a lower profile as the succession battle played out, has been described by fellow Ugandan journalists as quiet and humble. Besides the throne, the new king will inherit a considerable royal estate including swathes of land and sizeable cash payouts from the central government.

item.title: India-China relations, from conflict to cautious thaw
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold talks on Saturday on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping [USN:L1N4520BQ TEXT:"will hold talks"] on Saturday on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Here is a look at how ties between the Asian giants have evolved from a deadly 2020 border clash to a more stable footing today, as the Chinese leader makes his first visit to India in seven years. WHAT HAPPENED IN 2020? Indian and Chinese troops engaged in [USN:L1N3M10AB TEXT:"hand-to-hand combat"] in Galwan Valley in the Indian territory of Ladakh in the western Himalayas — their first deadly military confrontation since 1975 — after Indian soldiers set fire to two tents and observation towers they said were built on their side of the disputed border. At least 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed in the fighting in Galwan. The nuclear-armed neighbours share a roughly 3,800-km (2,400-mile), largely undemarcated and disputed border in the Himalayas. HOW DID THE GOVERNMENTS RESPOND? New Delhi [USN:L4N3ZY0YN TEXT:"increased scrutiny"] of Chinese investments, widened vetting of business visas for Chinese citizens, [USN:L4N2UQ1M1 TEXT:"banned"] popular Chinese mobile apps, and severed direct passenger air links. Beijing said the consensus between the countries had been seriously violated, and [USN:K7N36E01I TEXT:"tightened curbs"] on people-to-people exchanges, including the travel of journalists and businesspeople. WHEN DID DISENGAGEMENT HAPPEN? The neighbours [USN:L4N3LX0LS TEXT:"reached a disengagement pact "]in October 2024, by which point they had both pulled back troops from five locations where they had been facing off. The pact also entailed returning to the situation in 2020 by pulling back troops from the remaining two locations — a condition fulfilled by December that year. WHAT IS THE SITUATION NOW? Trade and business ties have improved, with New Delhi [USN:L1N3UB056 TEXT:"resuming direct flights"] to China, cutting red tape to [USN:L1N3XI06C TEXT:"speed approval"] of business visas for Chinese professionals, and [USN:L6N40I08D TEXT:"easing "][USN:L6N40I08D TEXT:"curbs"] on buying Chinese equipment. China was the South Asian nation's [USN:L6N43O08T TEXT:"largest source of imports"] in fiscal year 2025/26, worth $132 billion, including more than 100 products deemed critical to Indian factories. Along the frontier, though, both countries continue to maintain substantial [USN:L1N44M0IJ TEXT:"military deployments."] WHAT TENSIONS REMAIN? Besides [USN:L6N4490OG TEXT:"intermittent tension"] on the frontier, territorial disputes often flare over India's northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing calls Zangnan and considers a part of southern Tibet. China's role in India's military conflict last year with arch-rival Pakistan has also complicated ties. Although Beijing was not directly involved, Pakistan [USN:L6N3TC0L0 TEXT:"relied heavily"] on Chinese-made fighter jets and missiles during the four-day fighting. Trade ties also remain fragile, with industry executives highlighting visa delays and bottlenecks in procuring Chinese equipment and components critical in areas such as electronics and infrastructure development. India is also wary of Chinese investment in industries it considers sensitive for national security such as finance, defence and telecom.

item.title: Boca Juniors golea con doblete de paraguayo Romero y tanto de ecuatoriano Valencia en liga argentina
item.description: Un doblete del paraguayo Ángel Romero y otro tanto del ecuatoriano Enner Valencia le dieron a Boca Juniors el triunfo por 3-1 el viernes ante Central Córdoba en la novena jornada del torneo Clausura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un doblete del paraguayo Ángel Romero y otro tanto del ecuatoriano Enner Valencia le dieron a Boca Juniors el triunfo por 3-1 el viernes ante Central Córdoba en la novena jornada del torneo Clausura. "Me sentí muy bien, hace tiempo que no jugaba de titular, pero siempre trabajando para aprovechar la oportunidad. Fue una victoria importante”, dijo Romero a la televisión local. En el partido disputado en el estadio La Bombonera, Boca Juniors abrió el marcador al minuto cinco por intermedio de Romero luego de un centro del colombiano Sebastián Villa. El segundo gol del popular conjunto argentino llegó a los 11 minutos por intermedio de Valencia tras un centro bajo de Dylan Gorosito desde el sector derecho. En el segundo tiempo, Romero convirtió el tercer gol para Boca a los 56 minutos con un potente remate de larga distancia. Central Córdoba descontó a los 90 minutos por intermedio de Martín Cuitiño. “Nos llevamos tres puntos ante nuestra gente, y a medida que pasan los partidos me estoy adaptando a Boca. Esperemos que sea el primer gol de muchos", dijo Valencia tras su primer gol en el “Xeneize”. Por su parte, en el estadio Coloso-Marcelo Bielsa de la ciudad de Rosario en la provincia de Santa Fe, Newell's Old Boys rescató un agónico empate por 1-1 como local ante Vélez Sarsfield. Vélez abrió el marcador a los 27 minutos con un tanto del paraguayo Ronaldo Martínez, mientras que Newell's igualó a los 93 a través del ingresado Alan Soñora. El arquero de Vélez, Tomás Marchiori, atajó un penal a Santiago Solari a los 43 minutos, tras una mano de Simón Escobar dentro del área. En otro partido del viernes, Defensa y Justicia ganó por 2-0 como local a Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza con goles de Leandro Fernández y David Barbona.

item.title: Brewers demolish Reds 20-0, wrap up postseason berth
item.description: Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in six runs, and Dustin May tossed six innings of two-hit ball as the Milwaukee Brewers routed the visiting Cincinnati Reds 20-0 on Friday night to clinch their eighth postseason berth in nine seasons.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Garrett Mitchell hit a grand slam, William Contreras homered and drove in six runs, and Dustin May tossed six innings of two-hit ball as the Milwaukee Brewers routed the visiting Cincinnati Reds 20-0 on Friday night to clinch their eighth postseason berth in nine seasons. The Brewers fell short of the biggest shutout in modern major league history, a record they tied on Aug. 18 by trouncing the Seattle Mariners 22-0. May (7-9), acquired at the trade deadline from the St. Louis Cardinals, allowed singles in the first and fourth innings, both to Sal Stewart. May struck out six and walked one in an 84-pitch outing to improve to 2-2 with Milwaukee. Rookie Garrett Stallings pitched the final three innings for his first save. Mitchell's 10th homer of the year and first career grand slam capped an eight-run fifth that put the Brewers up 17-0. Brice Turang (3-for-3, four RBIs) and Jake Bauers homered during a six-run second when Milwaukee went in front 8-0. Contreras belted a three-run homer in the eighth off catcher Jose Trevino, who pitched the final two innings for the Reds. Milwaukee (92-56) pounded out a season-high 23 hits and won its fourth straight to maintain a 10-game lead in the National League Central over the Chicago Cubs (82-66), who won earlier Friday. The Brewers, bidding for their fourth consecutive division title, are 1 1/2 games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best overall record in the majors. The Brewers jumped on Andrew Abbott (6-11) for two runs in the first and six in the second, ending his outing after he allowed nine hits on 43 pitches. Cincinnati (69-78) has lost four straight. Contreras (sacrifice fly) and Andrew Vaughn (double) had the RBIs in the first inning. Cooper Pratt and Mitchell opened the second with consecutive singles. Jackson Chourio's one-out ground-rule double scored Pratt to make it 3-0. Turang then lined a 1-2 pitch 382 feet to right-center for a three-run homer. Vaughn singled with two outs, and Bauers followed with a 412-foot shot to center. Milwaukee added a run the fourth when Turang drew a leadoff walk and scored when Bauers' two-out single was misplayed for an outfield error. Rookie Luis Lara kept the Reds off the board in the fifth with a sensational leaping grab above the right field wall on Eugenio Suarez's potential homer. --Field Level Media

item.title: Orioles top Blue Jays, gain ground in wild-card chase
item.description: Dylan Beavers socked a solo home run and had three RBIs on Friday as the visiting Baltimore Orioles defeated the Toronto Blue Jays 7-4 to pick up a crucial game in the playoff chase.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Dylan Beavers socked a solo home run and had three RBIs on Friday as the visiting Baltimore Orioles defeated the Toronto Blue Jays 7-4 to pick up a crucial game in the playoff chase. Coby Mayo added a solo blast and Christian Encarnacion-Strand rapped out three hits for the Orioles in the opener of a three-game series. The Orioles (72-76) moved within one game of the Blue Jays (73-75) in the tight race for the third and final American League wild-card spot. The Cleveland Guardians (75-73), the current occupier of that slot, sit two games in front of Toronto and three games ahead of Baltimore after beating the Minnesota Twins 5-2 on Friday. Toronto's Brett Bateman hit his first major league homer, a two-run shot in the ninth against Alex Hoppe. After two singles followed, Rico Garcia got the final out to earn his eighth save. Kazuma Okamoto added a solo homer and double for the Blue Jays. The Orioles and Blue Jays are 4-4 in their season series with five games remaining between the teams. The winner of the season series would hold the tiebreaker for a playoff spot should it be needed. Beavers led off the game when he drove a homer to right against Max Scherzer (2-8) on an 0-1 cutter. Orioles starter Chris Bassitt (7-5), a former Blue Jay, survived a single and two walks in the home first. The rally was blunted when catcher Samuel Basallo picked off Vladimir Guerrero Jr. at first for the second out. The Orioles exploded for five runs in the second. Gunnar Henderson, Basallo and Encarnacion-Strand loaded the bases with no outs thanks to successive singles. Heston Kjerstad stroked an RBI single to right, Colton Cowser hit a two-run double to left and Beavers hit a two-run single to right before an out was recorded. Bassitt pitched around a bases-loaded jam after a single, an error and a walk in the third. Okamoto led off the Toronto fourth with a homer to right on a 1-0 sinker. Scherzer completed five innings, allowing six runs, seven hits and one walk with three strikeouts. Bassitt was replaced by Josh Walker after Toronto opened the sixth with a bloop single to left by Nathan Lukes and a ringing double to left by Okamoto. Andres Gimenez's one-out groundout to second off Josh Walker scored the only run of the inning. Bassitt allowed two runs, six hits and three walks with five strikeouts in five-plus innings. Mayo clubbed Braydon Fisher's 1-2 slider for a homer to left with two outs in the seventh. Bateman homered to right after Ernie Clement blooped a two-out double to right in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Carlos Rodon, Yankees beat Mets on 25th anniversary of 9/11
item.description: Carlos Rodon pitched 6 1/3 sharp innings and the host New York Yankees homered twice off rookie Nolan McLean in a 6-4 victory over the New York Mets on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Carlos Rodon pitched 6 1/3 sharp innings and the host New York Yankees homered twice off rookie Nolan McLean in a 6-4 victory over the New York Mets on Friday night. The Yankees (85-62) won for the ninth time in 12 games and 17th time in 24 games while moving closer to clinching their ninth postseason spot in the past 10 seasons. Cody Bellinger hit a tiebreaking three-run homer off McLean (11-9) in the second inning and Ben Rice added a leadoff blast in the fifth as the Yankees finished with 13 hits. Rookie Spencer Jones contributed an RBI single when the Yankees loaded the bases in the first and Ryan McMahon chipped in an RBI single in the eighth. In his longest start of a season interrupted by a pair of stints on the injured list with elbow injuries, Rodon (6-3) allowed two runs (one earned) on three hits. He struck out Juan Soto twice and finished with eight strikeouts overall while issuing one walk. Rodon exited to a nice ovation from the sellout crowd after allowing a single to rookie Carson Benge. Paul Blackburn loaded the bases and allowed an RBI single to rookie A.J. Ewing but Brent Headrick snagged Francisco Lindor's liner to escape a bases-loaded jam in the seventh. Headrick loaded the bases and was charged with a run in the eighth when Marcus Semien lifted a sacrifice fly off David Bednar. Bednar also allowed Ewing's homer to open the ninth before securing his 33rd save by retiring Soto on a 3-6-3 double play. There was a pregame ceremony to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, featuring various members of the team, including former captain Derek Jeter, Mariano Rivera and former manager Joe Torre. McLean allowed five runs and a career-high 10 hits in five innings. The right-hander struck out five, walked one and took his first loss in five starts as the Mets (68-79) had a four-game win streak snapped. McLean also allowed three or more earned runs for the third time in his past 18 starts and failed to complete six innings for the second time in his past 15 outings. After Christopher Morel delivered a game-tying RBI groundout in the second, Anthony Volpe and Rice singled with two outs before Bellinger hit a full-count curveball into the right field seats for his 14th homer. Rice extended the lead to 5-1 when he lifted McLean's first-pitch sinker into the left field seats for his 37th homer. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyle Tucker's slam carries Dodgers past Marlins for 8th straight win
item.description: Kyle Tucker went 3-for-3 with a grand slam and a season-high five RBIs, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to their eighth straight win, a 6-2 victory over the host Miami Marlins on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Tucker went 3-for-3 with a grand slam and a season-high five RBIs, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to their eighth straight win, a 6-2 victory over the host Miami Marlins on Friday. Tucker finished a double shy of the cycle. Los Angeles starter Blake Snell (4-1) struck out eight in 5 2/3 innings. He allowed one run on four hits and two walks, and he was removed after his pitch count reached 101. The Dodgers, who lead the National League West with a 90-57 record, played without injured power hitters Shohei Ohtani (right biceps) and Freddie Freeman (right knee). Miami (72-76) lost for the seventh time in eight games. Ryan Gusto (1-5) took a tough-luck defeat after producing a quality start. He lasted six innings and held the Dodgers to two runs on five hits and three walks. He fanned three. Miami's offense was led by Otto Lopez, who went 4-for-5. Javier Sanoja tripled, singled and scored twice. Los Angeles opened the scoring in the third inning. Tommy Edman drew a leadoff walk, advanced on Max Muncy's single and scored on Tucker's sacrifice fly. The Dodgers made it 2-0 in the sixth as Tucker tripled off the wall in right with one out and scored on Will Smith's bloop single to right. Miami got on the board in the sixth. Sanoja singled off Snell, stole second and scored on Agustin Ramirez's double off reliever Evan Phillips. Ramirez fouled off six pitches before lining a two-bagger to the gap in right-center. With two outs and no one on in the seventh, Edman drew a walk from Victor Vodnik. Muncy singled and Mookie Betts walked to load the bases. Miami brought in reliever Cade Gibson, whose third pitch was an 80 mph sweeper that Tucker pulled over the right field fence for his sixth career grand slam. Tucker hadn't hit a grand slam since 2023. Miami cut its deficit to 6-2 in the eighth when Sanoja tripled and scored on Owen Caissie's sacrifice fly. --Field Level Media

item.title: Royals make early lead hold, take series opener in Boston
item.description: Kansas City scored three runs over the first three innings and let its pitching do the rest as the Royals held on to beat the host Boston Red Sox 3-2 in their three-game series opener on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kansas City scored three runs over the first three innings and let its pitching do the rest as the Royals held on to beat the host Boston Red Sox 3-2 in their three-game series opener on Friday night. Carter Jensen (two doubles) went 2-for 5 with an RBI and Salvador Perez went 2-for-4 with an RBI to lead the Royals (66-82), who were just 3-7 in their previous 10 games. Seth Lugo (7-8) scattered seven hits and struck out seven across five innings of two-run ball for the victory. Steven Cruz finished off his seventh save with a 1-2-3 ninth. Mickey Gasper hit his ninth homer of the season and Wilyer Abreu went 2-for-4 with an RBI double for the Red Sox (80-68), who were held to just one hit over the final four innings. They have lost three straight since a five-game winning streak. The Royals jumped ahead with a pair of first-inning hits off Sonny Gray (17-5), who went six frames and allowed three runs on six hits. After Jensen crushed a leadoff double off the wall in deep center field, Perez knocked a two-out RBI single inside the third base line to open the scoring. After Gray responded with a 1-2-3 second, Isaac Collins and Jensen started the third with back-to-back doubles, extending Kansas City's lead to 2-0. Jensen's double high off the Green Monster brought in the run. Two batters later, Vinnie Pasquantino's single through the right side made it a three-run game before a double play ended the inning. The Red Sox wasted two singles in each of the first two innings and had baserunners in the first four, with Lugo posting inning-ending strikeouts in two of them. Gasper's one-out solo shot into the right-center field bullpen got the home team on the scoreboard in the fifth. After Adley Rutschman walked immediately following the homer, Abreu's RBI double high off the Monster brought the hosts within 3-2. Lugo stopped the threat there, striking out back-to-back batters. Nolan Hoffman and Connor Thomas relieved Lugo with back-to-back 1-2-3 innings, and Nate Pearson stranded Trevor Story on second base following a one-out double in the eighth. Story eluded second baseman Michael Massey's tag to reach safely. The Royals had a chance to extend their lead after Perez and Massey started the eighth with back-to-back singles, with Rutschman catching pinch runner Tyler Tolbert stealing second in between. Jovani Moran stranded two to end the inning before striking out two in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nationals' late rally upends Angels, halts 7-game slide
item.description: Jorbit Vivas hit a tiebreaking two-run double to cap a three-run eighth inning as the Washington Nationals snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 4-3 comeback victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels in the opener of a three-game series Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jorbit Vivas hit a tiebreaking two-run double to cap a three-run eighth inning as the Washington Nationals snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 4-3 comeback victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels in the opener of a three-game series Friday night. CJ Abrams had two hits and a run and James Wood went 1-for-3 with an RBI single and a walk for Washington (68-81). Clayton Beeter (6-5) tossed a scoreless eighth and Erik Tolman earned his second save despite allowing a run. Mike Trout hit a home run and Christian Moore doubled and had two hits and two RBIs for Los Angeles (56-91), which finished with just four hits. Samy Natera Jr. (1-2) allowed three runs on three hits and a walk in one inning for the Angels, who had won their previous two games. Los Angeles took a 1-0 lead in the first on Trout's 21st home run, a 416-foot drive to left-center. It snapped a 27-game homerless drought, one shy of his career high. It was also his 425th homer, moving him past Edwin Encarnacion into 54th place on the all-time list. Washington tied it in the fourth when Harry Ford walked, stole second and scored on Wood's two-out single to left. The Angels regained the lead in the seventh. Vaughn Grissom and Moises Ballesteros opened the inning with walks and Moore, after twice failing to move them along with a sacrifice bunt, singled to left on a 3-2 pitch to drive in Grissom for a 2-1 lead. The Nationals parlayed a leadoff walk by Brady House with three hits and a sacrifice fly to score three times in the eighth to go ahead 4-2. House correctly challenged a strike three call and worked a walk to open the inning. Abrams followed with a single, then Dylan Crews loaded the bases with a perfect bunt single up the third base line. After House was thrown out at home on a grounder hit by Yohandy Morales, pinch hitter Andrew Pinckney tied it at 2-2 with a sacrifice fly. After Morales stole second, Vivas followed with a two-run double into the right field corner to give the Nationals their first lead. The Angels came within about five feet of tying the game in the ninth when Moore drilled a two-out double off the top of the fence in right-center, driving in Oswald Peraza, who had walked. Tolman then got pinch hitter Kyren Paris to fly out to left to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: The evolution of BRICS and its challenges today
item.description: Leaders of the BRICS group of nations will meet on Saturday in the Indian capital of New Delhi for their annual summit, amid mounting geopolitical tension, disruptions in energy markets, shipping, and global trade.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Leaders of the BRICS group of nations will meet on Saturday in the Indian capital of New Delhi for their [USN:L1N4520BS TEXT:"annual summit"], amid mounting geopolitical tension, disruptions in energy markets, shipping, and global trade. Here is a look at the bloc's history, and the challenges it faces today. WHAT IS BRICS? The acronym BRIC was coined by Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Jim O'Neill in 2001, in a research paper highlighting the growth potential of Brazil, Russia, India, and China, but it was not until 2009 that the countries came together as a bloc. South Africa joined them in 2011, creating BRICS as it is known today. The grouping [USN:L1N3A50HL TEXT:"expanded"] in 2024, when Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE became members, and in 2025, when Indonesia joined. Saudi Arabia has also been invited to be part of the bloc but has not formally accepted the invitation. WHY WAS IT FORMED? BRICS was set up to challenge a world order dominated by the United States and its Western allies. Together, its members account for more than 40% of the world's population and almost a quarter of the global economy. The grouping today focuses on political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and people-to-people exchanges, according to the BRICS website set up by India during its presidency this year. Members meet annually, with the chairmanship rotating among them. WHAT HAS IT ACHIEVED? BRICS' biggest achievement is the multilateral New Development Bank, established in 2015 to finance infrastructure and sustainable development projects in emerging markets. The bank has approved 139 projects worth nearly $43 billion, according to its website, but suspended new transactions in Russia in the face of sanctions. In addition, a BRICS Pay System is being set up, with the aim of linking members' fast payment systems to enable cross-border settlements without relying on dollar-based banks. Members are also [USN:L1N44806L TEXT:"exploring linking"] their central bank digital currencies and are increasingly [USN:L1N45008Y TEXT:"settling trade"] in national currencies as they [USN:L8N4381GB TEXT:"pursue "][USN:L8N4381GB TEXT:"alternatives"] to dollar-based payment systems. WHAT ARE THE CHALLENGES? From disagreements on core purpose to divergent interests, BRICS is grappling with many challenges today. While Russia and China consider the bloc a counterweight to the West, India and Brazil see it as more focused on economics and reform. The 2024 expansion has also complicated its consensus-oriented approach, with divergent foreign policy interests hindering agreement. This hurdle will come into sharp focus this week, as India seeks to strike a joint statement by bridging differences between Tehran and Washington-ally Abu Dhabi, which are on opposing sides of the U.S.-Iran war. Their differences [USN:L1N41S0BA TEXT:"prevented a joint statement"] during the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi in May. HOW DOES THE WEST VIEW BRICS? Most Western nations are cautious about the grouping, recognising it as a platform that can slowly shift the balance of geopolitical power, but the bloc has repeatedly clashed with U.S. President Donald Trump, who has termed it "anti-American". He has also threatened to [USN:L1N3T50QB TEXT:"slap tariffs"] on its members if they try to set up a new BRICS currency, or back any currency to replace the U.S. dollar. Brazil floated the idea of a common BRICS currency during its chairmanship last year but the idea was later scrapped.

item.title: Junior Caminero's walk-off homer beats Astros, sends Rays to playoffs
item.description: Junior Caminero launched a mammoth walk-off home run in the ninth inning Friday night, sending the Tampa Bay Rays to the postseason by virtue of a 3-1 win over the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Junior Caminero launched a mammoth walk-off home run in the ninth inning Friday night, sending the Tampa Bay Rays to the postseason by virtue of a 3-1 win over the Houston Astros in St. Petersburg, Fla. The American League's home run leader, Caminero crushed a 417-foot blast to left-center field off reliever Bryan Abreu (6-4) for his 40th long ball. One batter earlier, Jonathan Aranda nearly homered to right-center, settling for a one-out double. Caminero then belted Abreu's 97 mph first-pitch fastball for his first career walk-off blast, making the Rays (88-59) the first club to clinch a postseason spot this year. The Rays, the American League East leaders who can get no worse than a wild card, are headed to the playoffs for the first time since 2023. Tampa Bay got a solo home run from Victor Mesa Jr., who also walked and stole a base. Richie Palacios recorded a single, a walk and a stolen base. Drew Rasmussen drew a no-decision after seven strong innings, though the Rays won for the 10th consecutive time in games he has started. The right-hander allowed one run on eight hits with four strikeouts and no walks in 92 pitches. Tampa Bay closer Bryan Baker (2-2) tossed a scoreless ninth inning with a walk and a strikeout. Without star slugger Yordan Alvarez, who twisted his right ankle running the bases Thursday in Philadelphia, the AL West-leading Astros (75-73) still outhit the Rays 9-4. Yainer Diaz went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a walk. Opener Miguel Ullola and Bryan King combined for 2 1/3 scoreless innings before Ethan Pecko took over as the bulk reliever. Pecko was sharp, yielding one run on one hit over 5 2/3 innings. He fanned four and walked two. In the fourth inning, Tampa Bay left fielder Chandler Simpson misplayed a one-out liner by Isaac Paredes for a double. Paredes, a former Ray, went to third on Daulton Varsho's single and scored on Diaz's fielder's-choice grounder for a 1-0 lead. After managing just one hit through four frames, the Rays pulled level when Mesa cranked Pecko's first pitch of the fifth for his 13th long ball. The shot to right-center off Pecko's four-seam fastball traveled 415 feet. --Field Level Media

item.title: BC LB Bodie Kahoun has movement in extremities after serious injury
item.description: Boston College linebacker Bodie Kahoun had to be taken off on a stretcher during the second quarter of the Eagles' game against Rutgers on Friday night in Chestnut Hill, Mass.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boston College linebacker Bodie Kahoun had to be taken off on a stretcher during the second quarter of the Eagles' game against Rutgers on Friday night in Chestnut Hill, Mass. Eagles coach Bill O'Brien said of Kahoun after his team's 28-21 win, according to the Boston Globe, "He's just an awesome guy. You can see what that meant to the team. ... It looks like there's some hope there with the feeling in his extremities." Kahoun made a tackle on Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond and remained down on the field before training staffs from both teams attended to him. After a delay of several minutes, Kahoun was transferred via stretcher into an ambulance to be taken off the field. Just before he was loaded in, he gave the crowd a thumbs-up. Boston College shared on social media that Kahoun "has movement in all extremities and is being taken to a local hospital for further examination." Kahoun is in his first season at Boston College after spending two years at Notre Dame. He had six tackles Friday before his injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Australia's Optus apologises for outage that disrupted emergency calls
item.description: Optus, Australia's No. 2 telecom carrier, on Saturday apologised a day after an outage on its network impacted users across three states and disrupted some emergency services calls.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Optus, Australia's No. 2 telecom carrier, on Saturday apologised a day after an outage on its network impacted users across three states and disrupted some emergency services calls. The 76-minute technical glitch on Friday affected Optus voice calling services in parts of Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania states and the Northern Territory, with some customers experiencing "intermittent call dropouts", Optus said in a statement. "We sincerely apologise to customers for the disruption," the statement said. The outage follows an Optus [USN:L3N3V800U TEXT:"network issue"] last year that left hundreds of people unable to contact police, fire and ambulance services and resulted in two deaths. Chris Bowen, a senior minister in the country's centre-left government, said it was "deeply concerning" that another outage had hit Optus customers. "All the necessary investigations have begun," Bowen said in televised remarks. "It's an obligation on our telecommunications companies to keep all their technology for triple-0 calls in the best possible working order." Police in Victoria said they completed around 40 welfare checks on callers hit by Friday's outage. "There were no adverse outcomes or issues of note," a police spokesperson said in a statement. In 2024, Optus, owned by Singapore Telecommunications (STEL.SI) , was fined A$12 million by regulators for failing to provide emergency call services to thousands during a nationwide outage in 2023. Optus also suffered a cyberattack in 2022 that affected the data of around 9.5 million Australians. (This story has been refiled to fix the grammar and the use of partial quote in paragraph 2.)

item.title: VinFast names founder's eldest son as its global chief executive
item.description: Vietnamese electric vehicle maker VinFast on Saturday named Chairman Pham Nhat Quan Anh, the eldest son of founder Pham Nhat Vuong, as its global chief executive as the loss-making firm plans a restructuring and overseas expansion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vietnamese electric vehicle maker VinFast (VFS.O) on Saturday named Chairman Pham Nhat Quan Anh, the eldest son of founder Pham Nhat Vuong, as its global chief executive as the loss-making firm plans a restructuring and overseas expansion. Anh, 33, who was [USN:L4N4220IT TEXT:"appointed global chairman"] in May, will also serve as chairman and chief executive officer of VinFast Vietnam. The EV maker is planning to restructure into a more [USN:L6N41Q0P5 TEXT:"asset-light company"] as it seeks growth in key markets such as Southeast Asia and [USN:L4N44Z0QJ TEXT:"India"]. "Pham Nhat Quan Anh will hold ultimate and comprehensive responsibility for all of VinFast's operations as the company enters a new phase of growth," the company said in a statement. Anh will succeed his father, founder Pham Nhat Vuong, as chief executive. Vuong will continue to serve on VinFast's board. Anh will be VinFast's fifth chief executive. Previous CEOs include former General Motors (GM.N) executive James DeLuca, ex-Opel chief Michael Lohscheller, and Le Thi Thu Thuy, who led the company through its Nasdaq listing. In May, VinFast [USN:L6N41R0QY TEXT:"unveiled a restructuring plan"] that would transfer manufacturing assets worth about $530 million to a purchaser group that would also take on about $6.9 billion in debt, as the automaker seeks to reduce future capital requirements. The complexity of the deal and the involvement of investors with ties to Vingroup (VIC.HM) and Vuong has raised concerns for some analysts and shareholders. VinFast reported a rise of nearly [USN:L4N42G132 TEXT:"42% in first-quarter revenue"] but posted a wider net loss. It has received ongoing financial support from Vuong, the founder and chairman of Vingroup, Vietnam's biggest conglomerate and VinFast's parent company. Anh is a graduate of Singapore Management University and held a number of senior roles at VinFast and other Vingroup companies before becoming chairman of VinFast Auto.
